credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Calif.io (security-disclosures@calif.io), in collaboration with Anthropic for reporting this issue.

affected.product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support

workarounds.value: Do not run untrusted applications in the affected Wayland session. Limit Wayland socket access for untrusted clients.

descriptions.value: A use-after-free flaw was found in mutter in the Wayland color-management ICC image-description path. A local attacker who can run a malicious Wayland client can destroy a wp_image_description_v1 resource while an asynchronous ICC file read is still in progress. cna.title: enclave-os-mini: RA-TLS challenge certificates were not bound to the TLS session

descriptions.value: Enclave OS Mini is a Rust-based runtime for confidential applications inside Intel SGX enclaves. Prior to wasm-v0.40.0, the SGX runtime's RA-TLS challenge certificate path placed the certificate public-key hash and client nonce in quote ReportData but omitted a value bound to the active TLS session. An attacker who obtained an enclave TLS private key could relay a genuine quote onto another connection, causing a relying party to accept an attacker-terminated connection as the attested enclave. This issue is fixed in wasm-v0.40.0.

A content author can store a link using a script-capable scheme, and a visitor who clicks the rendered link executes attacker-controlled script in the site's origin. cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema enum field defaults can inject statements into generated modules

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. modules: FUSE-T build for macOS: auxiliary FUSE-T mount and dismount handling (FuseService)

solutions.value: No fixed release as of 2026-10-11. A community fix exists as VeraCrypt pull request #1866 (commit 000bcf4): on dismount, explicitly shut down the auxiliary FUSE-T service through an authenticated control endpoint and wait for it to terminate before reporting the dismount as complete. The maintainer described the same approach in issue #1779. The macFUSE build of VeraCrypt is unaffected.

supportingMedia.value: No fixed release as of 2026-10-11. A community fix exists as VeraCrypt pull request #1866 (commit 000bcf4): on dismount, explicitly shut down the auxiliary FUSE-T service through an authenticated control endpoint and wait for it to terminate before reporting the dismount as complete. The maintainer described the same approach in issue #1779. The macFUSE build of VeraCrypt is unaffected.

references.name: Original public report (June 2026) with maintainer acknowledgment and diagnosis
Independent report with first process-level diagnosis and maintainer reply (June 2026)
Consolidated issue: reproductions, lsof evidence, kernel panic analysis, status
Community fix: terminate auxiliary FUSE-T service on dismount

workarounds.value: Use the macFUSE build of VeraCrypt instead of the FUSE-T build (the maintainer's recommended interim mitigation; the macFUSE build is not affected). If staying on the FUSE-T build: After dismounting your volumes, restart macOS to end any surviving sessions. Using the affected FUSE-T build again can recreate the problem. Updating FUSE-T alone hasn't been verified as a fix. A process name match can't reliably identify every surviving VeraCrypt service. Manual process killing shouldn't be treated as proof that access has ended, and killing a service while a volume is still mounted can interrupt writes.

descriptions.value: VeraCrypt 1.26.29 (FUSE-T build) on macOS sometimes allows unintended access to decrypted data. It does not terminate the FUSE-T auxiliary service (go-nfsv4) and its associated VeraCrypt core-service helper processes when a volume is dismounted. After VeraCrypt reports the volume as dismounted, the auxiliary mount continues to serve the decrypted volume image (volume.dmg) over a loopback SMB session, and the leaked processes retain an open handle to the underlying raw device. A local user or process can therefore remount and access the decrypted volume without the passphrase, e.g., by reopening a previously accessed path (such as through a macOS Open Recent menu) or by attaching volume.dmg from the stale auxiliary mount. (The macFUSE build of VeraCrypt is not affected.)

cna.title: Apache ActiveMQ, ActiveMQ Broker: The broker does not verify user provided connection id matches connection

descriptions.value:
Improper input validation vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ, Apache ActiveMQ KahaDB.



The ActiveMQ broker resolves connection, session and consumer state from ids that are user provided and in some scenarios does not validate that they ids are bound to that user. This allows an authenticated client to spoof another user's ids. This allows:





  *   an authenticated client consumes from another connection's temporary queue/topic by putting the victim's connection id in its own ConsumerId, bypassing the broker-side ownership check. 
  *  a duplicate ConsumerId registration is only logged, after which the attacker's RemoveInfo or disconnect tears down the victim's live subscription
  *  a forged MessageAck for the victim's ConsumerId permanently deletes an in-flight, unacknowledged message.








This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12; Apache ActiveMQ KahaDB: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.4.0, 6.3.3, or 5.19.12, which fixes the issue.

solutions.value: Fixed in commit a6da135 (PR #72) on the releases/stable-3.0 branch. 2.4 through 2.5.6 users should upgrade to 3.x, or backport the change to the two ngx_walk_tree() call sites in those versions.

workarounds.value: Restrict write access to the cache directories and all of their parent directories to the nginx user only, and do not run nginx and untrusted application code (for example PHP-FPM) as the same user. Remove any symbolic links found inside configured cache paths (find <cache_path> -type l). These measures also limit the similar traversal in nginx's own cache loader, which the fix in the module does not change.

supportingMedia.value: Restrict write access to the cache directories and all of their parent directories to the nginx user only, and do not run nginx and untrusted application code (for example PHP-FPM) as the same user. Remove any symbolic links found inside configured cache paths (find <cache_path> -type l). These measures also limit the similar traversal in nginx's own cache loader, which the fix in the module does not change.

descriptions.value: ngx_cache_purge before 3.0.4 can allow file deletion via a symlink attack in certain situations where nginx and a served application (e.g., WordPress) run under the same user account. The attacker must be able to create a symlink inside the cache path. Version 3.0.4 fixes this for the case of a symlink created at an arbitrary earlier time, but does not resolve an applicable TOCTOU race condition. (The ngx_cache_purge module follows symlinks while walking the cache directory tree during purge operations. The module relies on nginx's ngx_walk_tree(), which relies on stat() and therefore follows symlinks.)

configurations.value: nginx built with the ngx_cache_purge module and a proxy, fastcgi, scgi or uwsgi cache path with purge walks in use (purge_all, a wildcard purge, or cache_purge_vary_aware; arbitrary file deletion requires purge_all or a wildcard purge whose key reduces to an empty prefix), and an attacker able to create a symbolic link inside the cache path, for example when nginx and a web application run as the same user. The attacker does not need PURGE access: any legitimate purge of this kind, such as an automatic purge_all issued by a cache plugin, triggers the traversal.

descriptions.value:
Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in the HTTP/2 implementation of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust server CPU via small SETTINGS or connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE frames. The attacker opens thousands of streams whose responses block on the connection send window, then sends cheap frames that each make the server walk the whole queue of blocked sends. In the reporter's run, with 3,000 blocked streams a single 9-byte SETTINGS frame took 133 ms to process.

do_pending_sends/2 in lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex retries every queued send and, before each retry, removes that entry from the queue with List.delete/2, so one frame costs O(n²) list operations for n blocked streams. max_concurrent_streams defaults to :infinity, so the attacker chooses n.

This issue affects bandit: from 0.3.4 before 1.14.0.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* On one HTTP/2 connection, send 3,000 requests to an endpoint with a 20 KB response body, and send no connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE, so the responses queue in pending_sends.
* Send an empty SETTINGS frame followed by a PING.
* Time the PING acknowledgement. In the reporter's run, the single 9-byte SETTINGS frame delayed it by 133 ms. Repeating the frame keeps the connection process busy.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Blocked sends

A response that outruns the connection send window is queued in pending_sends. With max_concurrent_streams defaulting to :infinity and no connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE from the client, every one of n streams ends up queued.

2. Trigger (lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex)

Every non-ACK SETTINGS frame and every WINDOW_UPDATE on stream 0 calls do_pending_sends/2. SETTINGS handling also sends deliver_send_window_update to every stream even when the window delta is 0, so unread messages pile up in the mailboxes of blocked streams.

3. Quadratic drain

do_pending_sends/2 walks the queue and calls List.delete/2 on the whole list before retrying each entry, putting it back at the front if the send is still blocked. One frame therefore costs O(n²) list operations, about 10^8 at n = 10,000.

cna.title: Model Context Protocol Java SDK HTTP server transports allow memory exhaustion through unbounded request bodies

descriptions.value: The Model Context Protocol Java SDK is the official Java SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From version 0.8.0 through 0.12.0 in the io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp artifact, from 0.13.0 through 0.18.3 and 1.0.0 through 1.1.3 in io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp-core, and from mcp-core 2.0.0-M1 through 2.0.0, the Servlet-based SSE, Streamable HTTP, and Stateless server transports read an HTTP request body into memory without enforcing a maximum size. An unauthenticated remote client able to reach an affected transport can stream an arbitrarily large POST body, including with chunked transfer encoding, until the Java process exhausts its heap and becomes unavailable. Authentication, Origin or Host validation, or an upstream request-size limit can reject the request before the vulnerable read. The maintained mcp-core lines are fixed in versions 0.18.4, 1.1.4, and 2.0.1.

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via ISO-2022 Escape Sequences Allows XXE and Denial of Service

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, XmlScanner::scan in src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php uses a DOCTYPE detection pattern that accounts for NUL-byte interleaving but not ISO-2022 escape sequences in XLSX XML parts. The escape sequences prevent the scanner from matching the declaration, and XML charset normalization then removes the escape bytes before parsing, exposing a valid DOCTYPE and entity definitions. Processing an attacker-controlled XLSX can therefore cause entity-expansion denial of service on supported PHP versions and can permit local file access or SSRF on PHP before 8.0 or when LIBXML_NOENT is enabled. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')

cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema fixed namespaces allow code injection in generated annotations

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.38.0 through 0.70.5, BaseGenerator.parse_fixed inserts a fixed type's namespace value between quotes inside a generated types.confixed annotation without escaping or validating it. A crafted quote can terminate the namespace string and alter the surrounding annotation expression, which Python evaluates when the generated class is defined, allowing arbitrary code execution. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by requiring the namespace to be a dot-separated sequence of valid Avro names.

workarounds.value: Until a fixed release is available, restrict HTTPRoute creation and modification for routes attached to the shared Gateway, and review or remove routes with match values that trigger the predicate injection. Where possible, enforce authentication and rate limiting at the backend as additional controls. An admission policy could reject confirmed exploit patterns, but validate it against legitimate routes; Gateway API match values can contain special characters. These measures reduce exposure but do not fix the shim. The backend and admission-policy measures are compensating controls; their effectiveness depends on the deployment and the specific route behavior

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the internal WebAssembly (WASM) shim used by the Kuadrant operator. When generating the CEL predicate that determines whether Gateway-level authentication and rate limiting should run, the shim does not correctly escape values from HTTPRoute match fields. A user who can create or modify an HTTPRoute attached to a shared Gateway can provide a crafted path, header, or query match value that causes the predicate to skip those checks. The request is still forwarded to the route’s backend.

descriptions.value: Wizarr is an advanced user invitation and management system for Jellyfin, Plex, Emby, and other media servers. Prior to 2026.9.1, wizard step Markdown supplied through the editor or imported bundles was evaluated by app/blueprints/wizard/routes.py in the application's non-sandboxed Jinja2 environment with application globals exposed. An authenticated user able to create steps, or an administrator importing an untrusted bundle through POST /settings/wizard/import, could execute arbitrary Python when GET /wizard/{server}/{idx} rendered the stored step; app/jinja_filters.py and app/services/wizard_widgets.py contained additional evaluation sinks. This could execute operating-system commands as the application user, disclose the Flask SECRET_KEY, access connected service credentials and the database, and produce stored cross-site scripting. cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via Double-Encoded unentity() TOCTOU Allows XXE and Denial of Service

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. From 3.3.0 until 3.10.8 and 5.10.0, Reader\Xml passes stored SpreadsheetML XML through XmlScanner::scan in Xml::canRead and Xml::trySimpleXMLLoadStringPrivate, while Xml::unentity decodes numeric entities only after each DOCTYPE pattern check. A double-encoded less-than character is reduced by the first callback to another encoded character and by the second callback to a literal less-than sign, so SimpleXML receives an unchecked DOCTYPE and entity declaration. Processing attacker-controlled SpreadsheetML XML can cause entity-expansion denial of service and can permit local file access or SSRF on PHP before 8.0 or when LIBXML_NOENT is enabled. This issue is fixed in versions 3.10.8 and 5.10.0.

cna.title: DBI versions before 1.656 for Perl crash via type confusion in dbi_profile when a database handle is destroyed under a Profile Path with an {attr} element

solutions.value: Upgrade to DBI 1.656 or later.

descriptions.value:
DBI versions before 1.656 for Perl crash via type confusion in dbi_profile when a database handle is destroyed under a Profile Path with an {attr} element.

An {attr} element names a database handle attribute, which dbi_profile reads from the handle's inner hash. It expects the inner handle as a reference and dereferences it, but a handle that is being destroyed hands back the inner hash itself, so the dereference yields the hash's bucket array. A type check on that pointer usually fails and the call goes unprofiled. When the memory it addresses passes the check, the attribute lookup dereferences a NULL or invalid pointer and the process dies on SIGSEGV.

The Path is set by the application, by the Profile handle attribute, or by the DBI_PROFILE environment variable, so `DBI_PROFILE={ImplementorClass}` can crash an unmodified program.

descriptions.description: CWE-843 Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

Authentication bypass within in-house network in Apache Kylin. Impact most to the kylin services that are directly exposed to public network, which is not common. In-house kylin deployments are mostly not impacted.



This issue affects Apache Kylin: from 4.0.4 through 5.0.4.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 5.0.5, which fixes the issue.

descriptions.value: Spreadsheet formula injection in conversion-tracking report exports in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to submit conversion values that are written as formulas instead of text in an XLS workbook. When a user opens the exported report in a spreadsheet application, attacker-supplied formulas can be evaluated. The confirmed impact is formula execution within the workbook; disclosure of information to the attacker has not been established. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by sanitising conversion values before writing them to the affected XLS report sections.

cna.title: temporal-proxy payload decryption is not bound to the request namespace

credits.value: Reported internally at Temporal Technologies, Inc.
Praetorian, who independently reported this issue responsibly to Temporal Technologies

descriptions.value: Disclosure, across the namespace authorization boundary, of payloads the proxy encrypted: Workflow and Activity inputs and results, and Signal and Update arguments. Encrypted payloads cannot be modified through this issue, and data the proxy does not encrypt is not affected. No availability impact was identified.

solutions.value: Upgrade to temporal-proxy 0.9.0 or later and set encryption.namespaceBinding to strict. Fixed releases record the namespace in each payload they encrypt and, in strict mode, refuse to decrypt a payload recorded for another namespace or for none, including through the codec server's /decode endpoint, which then requires the caller to name a namespace. The setting has no default and must be set whenever encryption keys are configured. The off and permissive modes exist to migrate payloads encrypted by earlier releases, which carry no namespace, and do not close this issue; move to strict once the vault_unbound_opens_total and vault_namespace_mismatches_total metrics have stayed at zero for longer than namespace retention. Payloads carried in Nexus operations are not compared, because they cross namespaces by design.

references.name: Vault.Open in temporal-proxy 0.8.0, which takes no namespace
KEKRegistry.Decrypt in temporal-proxy 0.8.0, which selects the KEK by the identifier in the payload
AES-256-GCM sealed and opened with no associated data in temporal-proxy 0.8.0
Design discussion of associated data in the payload encryption scheme

workarounds.value: Until a fixed release is deployed, serve namespaces that must stay isolated from each other through separate proxy deployments, or use KMS key policies that let each proxy use only the keys of the namespaces it serves. Giving each namespace its own key on a single proxy does not help, because that proxy holds all of them. Leaving the codec server disabled closes the /decode route only.

descriptions.value: temporal-proxy 0.2.0 through 0.8.0 does not bind encrypted payloads to the namespace they were encrypted for. When payload encryption is enabled, the proxy chooses the decryption key by an identifier stored in the payload rather than by the namespace of the request, and nothing in the ciphertext records that namespace. A caller whom the proxy authorizes only for namespace B, and who has obtained an encrypted payload from namespace A, can therefore have the proxy decrypt it. In 0.8.0, the caller can submit the payload to the codec server's /decode endpoint. In every affected version, a caller who can also write to namespace B on the Temporal server directly can place the payload there and read it back through the proxy. This holds whether namespaces share the default key or each has its own, because a single proxy holds every key it is configured with. The issue does not give the attacker encrypted payloads they could not already obtain, and does not allow encrypted payloads to be modified.

descriptions.description: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

configurations.value: Exploitation requires all of the following. Payload encryption is enabled; it is off by default. Callers are restricted to particular namespaces, either by an authorization extension (0.5.0 and later) or by per-namespace authorization on the upstream Temporal server. The attacker is authorized for one namespace and holds an encrypted payload from another, obtained outside the proxy, for example through read access on the Temporal server, an export, or the persistence store. Either the codec server is enabled (0.8.0 only, off by default), or the attacker can write to their own namespace on the Temporal server directly. In affected versions, the built-in static-token and JWKS authenticators do not restrict callers by namespace, so a deployment that relies on them alone already lets every caller read every namespace through the proxy, and this issue crosses no further boundary there.

cna.title: Xerial snappy-java before 1.1.10.9 Unbounded Memory Allocation Denial of Service

credits.value: Yu Bao, PayPal Cyber Security Team

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Xerial snappy-java before 1.1.10.9 Unbounded Memory Allocation Denial of Service

descriptions.value: Xerial snappy-java before 1.1.10.9 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability that allows attackers to exhaust JVM memory by declaring a large uncompressed length in compressed input. Attackers can supply a few crafted bytes to Snappy.uncompress, uncompressString, SnappyInputStream or SnappyFramedInputStream to force allocations up to 2 GB, causing OutOfMemoryError and denial of service.

descriptions.description: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

cna.title: Apache ActiveMQ, ActiveMQ Broker: Repeated rejected temporary destination consumer requests can lead to broker OOM

descriptions.value:
Denial of Service via OOM vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ, ActiveMQ Broker.



An authenticated OpenWire client that sends a ConsumerInfo for a temporary queue/topic owned by another connection is rejected with InvalidDestinationException, but the rejected Subscription is left behind in the region's subscriptions map. Repeating the request leaks broker heap until OOM because the broker does not clean up the rejected subscriptions in the map.



This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12; ActiveMQ Broker: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.4.0, 6.3.3, or 5.19.12, which fixes the issue.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Wukong AICRM through 20260610 Authorization Bypass via User-Controlled Session ID in POST /chat/send

descriptions.value: Wukong AICRM through 20260610 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write into other users' AI chat sessions by supplying an arbitrary sessionId to POST /chat/send. Attackers can append messages to a victim's conversation and receive streamed assistant replies built from the victim's last 20 messages, disclosing conversation content.

cna.title: Pingvin Share X before 1.22.0 Ineffective Authentication Rate Limiting via Throttler TTL

Unauthenticated attackers can send effectively unthrottled requests to /api/auth/signIn, /api/auth/signIn/totp and /api/auth/resetPassword to brute-force passwords and TOTP codes.

cna.title: Improper Authentication and Credential Exposure in Multiple TP-Link Kasa Devices

credits.value: M. Hammad Mazhar from University of Northern Colorado & Madeline Cooreman

descriptions.value: CAPEC-115 Authentication Bypass

Multiple
Kasa devices contain an improper authentication vulnerability in the local
device-management protocol. An unauthenticated adjacent attacker may send
management instructions to an affected device without adequate authentication
or authorization, allowing modification of the device state or management
settings. Under certain usage conditions involving interaction between the
user, mobile application, and device-cloud service, insufficient protection of
account-related communications may also expose account information.









Successful
exploitation may allow an unauthenticated adjacent-network attacker to perform
unauthorized device-management actions and disrupt legitimate user control.
Under certain conditions, account-related information may also be exposed,
potentially leading to compromise of the associated cloud account.

cna.title: Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header

descriptions.value:
Symfony is a PHP framework for web and console applications and a set of reusable PHP components. Prior to versions 5.4.54, 6.4.46, 7.4.19, and 8.1.7, HeaderUtils::split() parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a (?<!\s) lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. HeaderBag calls it for the Cache-Control header whenever a Request is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.



A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, preg_match_all() gives up at pcre.backtrack_limit and split() returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.



This issue affects symfony/http-foundation v4.1.0-BETA1 through v5.4.53, v6.0.0-BETA1 through v6.4.45, v7.0.0-BETA1 through v7.4.18, and v8.0.0-BETA1 through v8.1.6.

cna.title: Apache Roller: Stored cross-site scripting through AtomPub entry tags

descriptions.value: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 5.0.1 through 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog to store script in entry tags submitted through AtomPub. Roller's tag filter allowed HTML characters in tag names, and the bundled gaurav, fauxcoly and frontpage themes and the showEntryTags macro print tag names without escaping, so the script runs in the browser of anyone who views the weblog. This matters when weblog authors are not trusted with script (weblogAdminsUntrusted=true, the default since 6.1.4). AtomPub is disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which removes HTML characters from tag names, including names stored earlier.

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: SSRF whitelist bypass via unre-validated HTTP redirect in Drawing::setPath external image loading

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, Worksheet\Drawing::setPath validates only the initial external-image URL with setIsWhitelisted when setAllowExternalImages is enabled. The HTTP stream context permits PHP to follow a redirect without applying the callback to the redirected URL, so a permitted image host can redirect the server to an internal address and cause a blind GET request. The response body is not returned to the attacker because the reader validates the downloaded content as an image and removes the temporary file, but internal GET-driven endpoints, network reachability, and cloud metadata endpoints may be reached. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

cna.title: dataclasses-avroschema record documentation can terminate generated class docstrings

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.40.0 through 0.70.5, ClassRepresentation.render_docstring copies a schema record's doc value into a generated triple-double-quoted class docstring without escaping quotes or backslashes. A crafted triple-quote sequence can close the docstring and inject statements into the generated class body, while a trailing backslash can escape the generated closing delimiter, allowing Python code execution during module import. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by escaping quotes, backslashes, and unsafe control characters before rendering docstrings.

cna.title: Inadequate authorization vulnerability in Alosuite’s user invitation functionality

descriptions.value: CAPEC-233 Privilege Escalation

solutions.value: The manufacturer has indicated that the vulnerabilities have been fixed in version 26_04_15.03_10 of ALO Suite, released in April 2026. It is recommended that you use the patched version.

supportingMedia.value: The manufacturer has indicated that the vulnerabilities have been fixed in version 26_04_15.03_10 of ALO Suite, released in April 2026. It is recommended that you use the patched version.

descriptions.value: Inadequate authorization vulnerability in Alosuite’s user invitation functionality. The ‘/Requests/userInvitation’ endpoint does not properly validate the assignment of privileges on the server, allowing an attacker to manipulate the invitation parameters during the request process. By intercepting and modifying a legitimate invitation request, an unauthenticated attacker can assign administrative privileges to a newly invited user without the appropriate authorization checks. A successful exploit results in unauthorized privilege escalation, granting full administrative access to the affected application.

supportingMedia.value: Inadequate authorization vulnerability in Alosuite’s user invitation functionality. The ‘/Requests/userInvitation’ endpoint does not properly validate the assignment of privileges on the server, allowing an attacker to manipulate the invitation parameters during the request process. A successful exploit results in unauthorized privilege escalation, granting full administrative access to the affected application.

cna.title: Apache CXF: Prevent unbounded XML document size in StaxUtils by adding default element and character limits

descriptions.value:
By default, StaxUtils placed no limit on the total number of elements or the total number of characters in an XML document. A very large request could therefore use a lot of memory and CPU during parsing, especially where CXF builds a DOM from the input (for example SAAJ or WS-Security), and could cause a denial of service when no request size limit was configured. Both limits now have defaults: the maximum element count is 100 × maxChildElements (5,000,000 by default), and the maximum document size is 256M characters. Applications that process larger documents can raise the limits with the org.apache.cxf.stax.maxElementCount and org.apache.cxf.stax.maxXMLCharacters properties.
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

cna.title: TinaCMS admin preview iframe loads an attacker-controlled origin from the URL fragment

descriptions.value: Tina is a headless content management system. Prior to tinacms 3.14.0 and @tinacms/app 2.5.14, the /~/* admin preview route in packages/tinacms/src/admin/index.tsx can turn an attacker-controlled hash-router splat into an off-origin iframe URL through packages/@tinacms/app/src/preview.tsx, while packages/@tinacms/app/src/lib/preview-origin.ts derives expectedOrigin from that same URL for the GraphQL message channel in packages/@tinacms/app/src/lib/graphql-reducer.ts. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted link to a signed-in editor, cause the admin to frame an attacker origin, and have that frame treated as the trusted preview. The attacker-controlled frame can submit GraphQL reads or mutations that the admin executes with the editor credentials, exposing or modifying protected content. This issue is fixed in tinacms 3.14.0 and @tinacms/app 2.5.14.

cna.title: Shiny for Python - Path traversal in bookmark restore

descriptions.value: Shiny for Python is a framework for building interactive web applications in Python. From 1.4.0 until 1.6.4, bookmark restore accepts a client-supplied state_id and joins it into the server-side shiny_bookmarks directory without validating that it is a single safe path segment. An unauthenticated request can use parent-directory segments or an absolute path to make the server open input.json and values.json outside the bookmark store, even when bookmark_store is set to disable. In applications configured with bookmark_store set to server and using ui.input_file(), the restore handler can additionally copy and expose an attacker-selected file from an attacker-selected directory. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.4.

cna.title: Busybox: busybox: tar extraction-root escape via deferred symlink/hardlink creation bypasses cve-2026-26158 fix

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank TAE3 for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Avoid extracting tar archives from untrusted sources using busybox, especially with elevated privileges or into a directory that will be reused for a subsequent extraction. If untrusted archives must be processed, extract into a freshly created, isolated directory with minimal privileges on a single filesystem boundary and discard it (including any links left on disk) after each extraction.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in busybox. The tar applet's deferred link-creation handling for symlink and hardlink entries with unsafe-looking targets does not validate that the resolved destination remains inside the extraction directory once the deferred link is created. An attacker can craft a tar archive using a symlink target of exactly '..' combined with a deferred hardlink to create a new file outside the extraction directory, or reuse an extraction directory across two archives to replace an existing file outside it. If the archive is extracted with elevated privileges, this flaw can lead to privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet ODS Reader: Unbounded number-rows-repeated → CPU & Memory Exhaustion (DoS)

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, Ods::processTableRow in src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Ods.php accepts an unbounded table:number-rows-repeated attribute from an ODS table row. When the row contains a value, the reader materializes a cell for every repetition without checking the spreadsheet row limit, so a small attacker-controlled ODS file can consume substantial CPU and memory and terminate the PHP worker. Column repetition is separately bounded and is not part of this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-125 Flooding

solutions.value: The manufacturer has indicated that the vulnerabilities have been fixed in version 26_04_15.03_10 of ALO Suite, released in April 2026. It is recommended that you use the patched version.

descriptions.value: Vulnerability due to a lack of request limits in Alosuite’s password recovery functionality. The ‘/Account/resetPwd’ endpoint does not enforce adequate restrictions on the number or frequency of password reset requests sent for a single account. As a result, a remote attacker can repeatedly call the endpoint to generate an unlimited number of password reset emails addressed to a user, causing an email flood and enabling abuse of the password recovery mechanism. The absence of request limits or other controls against automation can harm legitimate users, consume application and email infrastructure resources, and facilitate automated attacks against the password recovery service.

cna.title: Privasys rustls fork: RA-TLS challenge mode did not bind attestation evidence to the TLS session

descriptions.value: Privasys rustls is a maintained fork of the rustls TLS library that adds RA-TLS challenge and channel-binding support. Prior to privasys-v0.8.1, the fork emitted RA-TLS challenge certificates whose quote ReportData was bound to the certificate public key and client nonce but not to the active TLS session. An attacker who obtained an enclave TLS private key could relay a genuine quote onto another connection, causing a relying party to accept an attacker-terminated connection as the attested enclave. This issue is fixed in privasys-v0.8.1.

cna.title: Code execution through web query files given on the command line

descriptions.value: CAPEC-242 Code Injection

LibreOffice can open a web query file (.iqy), which names a web page to import into a spreadsheet, when the file is given on its command line, for example when a file manager or another program opens the file with LibreOffice. The address in such a file was used without the checks that apply to an address given on the command line directly, so a crafted file could make LibreOffice do something other than open a web page, up to running code. In fixed versions only an http or https address is taken from a web query file.

descriptions.description: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

descriptions.value: dataclasses-avroschema generates Avro schemas from Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, and Faust Records and generates Python code from Avro schemas. From version 0.38.0 through 0.70.5, EnumRepresentation.render_symbols concatenates each schema-controlled enum symbol between double quotes in a generated enum assignment. When generator classes are used directly, a quote can terminate the string literal and inject arbitrary Python code into the enum class body, which executes when the generated module is imported. Version 0.70.6 fixes the vulnerability by escaping enum symbol values before rendering them.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in the HTTP/2 implementation of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust server memory via DATA frames sent past the advertised receive window. The attacker requests a response larger than the 65,535-byte initial window and withholds WINDOW_UPDATE, so the stream process blocks while sending and stops reading, then floods small DATA frames on that stream. Every frame is queued in the stream's mailbox until the BEAM node runs out of memory.

Bandit.HTTP2.Connection.handle_frame/3 in lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex forwards each DATA frame to the stream process without consulting the receive window, and Bandit.HTTP2.FlowControl.compute_recv_window/2 replenishes the window as data arrives rather than as it is consumed, and never answers a violation with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.

This issue affects bandit: from 0.3.1 before 1.14.0.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* On an HTTP/2 connection, request a resource whose response exceeds 65,535 bytes and send no WINDOW_UPDATE. The server sends one window's worth and the stream blocks in send_data/3.
* Send 1-byte DATA frames on that stream in batches, ignoring the server's receive windows.
* Between batches, at intervals under 15 seconds, send a stream WINDOW_UPDATE with an increment of 1 to keep the blocked send alive.
* Send a PING. It is acknowledged, and the server has sent neither FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR nor GOAWAY while its memory grows with every frame.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Connection-level window (lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex, lib/bandit/http2/flow_control.ex)

The handle_frame/3 clause for DATA frames sends the payload to the stream process before any window is checked. It then calls compute_recv_window/2, which subtracts the frame size and, once the window drops below 2^30, advertises a WINDOW_UPDATE back up to 2^31-1. A negative window is accepted, so a peer that overruns the window is never refused, and the window refills when data arrives rather than when it is consumed.

2. Stream-level window (lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex)

The stream receive window is debited only when the stream process reads the DATA message, and it never rejects a violation either.

3. Accumulation

While send_data/3 waits for send window, its selective receive matches only window updates and resets, so DATA messages pile up unread in the mailbox. A stream WINDOW_UPDATE of 1 byte, sent at intervals under the 15-second send timeout, keeps the stream alive while the attacker floods 1-byte DATA frames.

cna.title: Robots::Validate versions from 0.4.3 before 0.4.10 for Perl report clients as imposter robots when User-Agent matcher state carries over from a previous request

solutions.value:
Upgrade to Robots-Validate v0.4.10 or later.

Deployments with Algorithm::AhoCorasick::XS should upgrade to v0.4.11, which fixed a bug with using that version.

descriptions.value:
Robots::Validate versions from 0.4.3 before 0.4.10 for Perl report clients as imposter robots when User-Agent matcher state carries over from a previous request.

Each Robots::Validate object holds one pure-Perl Aho-Corasick search machine and feeds every User-Agent into it without resetting its state. A User-Agent that ends part-way through a robot name leaves the machine mid-match, so the next User-Agent checked by the same object can complete that name. That client's address is then checked against the robot's DNS rule, which it fails.

A remote client can use this to make a site that blocks bad robots block other visitors where the prefix User-Agent string is a suffix of a robot being validated.

Note that deployments with Algorithm::AhoCorasick::XS are also affected, since it was unused due to a different bug.

Until an upgrade can be applied, Bizerba recommends implementing the following measures:

·         Delete BRAIN2 installation log files after successful installation.

·         Restrict administrative access to affected systems.

·         Ensure temporary directories containing installation artifacts are adequately protected.

·         Change the password of the configured service account if credential exposure is suspected.

Administrators should review and remove setup log files following the naming convention:

Bizerba BRAIN2_<Version>_<InstallationDate>_<InstallationTime>_setup.log

descriptions.value:
A vulnerability has been identified in
BRAIN2 versions up to and including version 3.09. Under specific installation
conditions, the password of a Windows service account may be written in
cleartext to a setup log file. The issue occurs when Microsoft SQL Server
access is configured using Integrated Security and the Windows account intended
to run the BRAIN2 MainService is specified during execution of the BRAIN2
installation wizard. The setup log file is stored in the
temporary directory of the Windows administrator performing the installation.
This directory is not accessible to standard Windows users and can generally
only be accessed by users with administrative privileges. Successful exploitation could result in the
disclosure of credentials belonging to the configured BRAIN2 service account.

cna.title: Docker Desktop WSL2 AF_VSOCK isolation bypass via 32-bit socketcall

solutions.value: Upgrade to Docker Desktop 4.98.0 or later and WSL 3.0.3 or later. Both are required.

references.name: Microsoft WSL kernel 6.18.54.1 dependency release notes

descriptions.value: In Docker Desktop for Windows with the WSL2 backend, an unprivileged Linux container can use 32-bit socketcall to bypass the default seccomp restriction on AF_VSOCK. This can expose host-facing services and Windows files accessible to the logged-in user. The issue affects x86-64 WSL2; LinuxKit-based backends are unaffected. cna.title: filelock: StrictSoftFileLock follows a symbolic link swapped in at <path>.filelock and creates claim files in a directory another local user chooses

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.30.0 until 4.2.1, On POSIX platforms, StrictSoftFileLock and AsyncStrictSoftFileLock validate the coordination directory in _ensure_protocol_directory but later reach the claims directory through _open_directory by pathname, allowing a local account that can rename the coordination name to swap in a symbolic link between check and use during acquisition. That race can create and leave claim files in another writable directory or strand claims in a different strict lock so the second lock times out. Separately, the claims property and force_break follow a resting symbolic link without a race when the lock user inspects or recovers the lock. Claims inspection discloses a file name to the other account only if the resulting exception text or claim_name reaches that account through a shared log, CI output, or error report. A blind force_break recovery that removes live claims from another strict lock can allow two processes into that lock's critical section; this path reaches other strict locks, not arbitrary files. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix extends the BLOCKED_RANGES list in is_safe_url() to include the previously missing IP address ranges: 0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, ::/128, fc00::/7, and fe80::/10. Regression tests are added covering both literal IP addresses in URLs and hostnames that resolve to the newly blocked ranges.
assumptions: PR:L assumes that creating or modifying a MISP attribute to trigger the html_to_markdown expansion module requires authenticated access. MISP typically enforces authentication for attribute operations, but the patch does not explicitly state the authentication model.

SC:H assumes the MISP server can reach internal services (e.g., cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, internal admin panels, or CGNAT infrastructure) and that the responses are returned to the attacker via the Markdown conversion output. The actual impact depends on the server's network topology.
The exact affected version range is not specified in the patch. The nearest tag is v3.0.13 with 139 commits after the fix, but the precise release containing the fix is not identified.
CAPEC-12 is selected as the closest match; no alternative CAPEC more precisely describes an SSRF via incomplete IP-range validation in a URL-fetching module.

The patch does not indicate whether the module follows redirects to additional unblocked ranges; MAX_REDIRECTS is set to 10, and the redirect target validation is not shown in this patch. If redirect targets are not re-validated, the SSRF surface may be broader than what this patch addresses.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In misp_modules/modules/expansion/html_to_markdown.py, five new ipaddress.ip_network() entries are added to the BLOCKED_RANGES list: 0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, ::/128, fc00::/7, and fe80::/10. In tests/test_html_to_markdown.py, two new test methods are added: test_blocks_unspecified_shared_ula_and_link_local_literals verifies that is_safe_url() returns False for literal URLs using each blocked range (including IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms), and test_blocks_hostnames_resolving_to_ula_addresses verifies that a hostname resolving to an fc00::/7 address is rejected.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The vulnerable URL is supplied via a MISP attribute over the network. AC:L: Crafting a URL with a blocked-range IP is straightforward; no race or special timing is needed. AT:N: No manipulation of the target service is required. PR:L: Creating or modifying a MISP attribute that triggers the expansion module requires authenticated access (assumed; MISP typically requires authentication for attribute operations). UI:N: No victim interaction beyond the initial attribute creation is needed. VC:N, VI:N, VA:N: The MISP server itself is not compromised; it is used as a proxy. SC:H: The SSRF allows reading responses from internal services (e.g., cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels), representing a high confidentiality impact on the target system. SI:N, SA:N: The module performs a GET-style fetch for HTML-to-Markdown conversion; no evidence of write or security-impact on the target.

capecRationale.rationale: The patch directly addresses an SSRF condition: the application fetches a URL on behalf of the user, and the validation logic failed to block requests to internal and restricted IP ranges. An attacker crafts a URL with a blocked-range IP (e.g., http://0.0.0.0/admin or http://[fe80::1]/) to cause the MISP server to issue a request to an internal service. This is the canonical CAPEC-12 pattern. No uncertainty in this mapping.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The html_to_markdown module fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The incomplete IP range allow/block list permitted requests to internal, link-local, and otherwise restricted network destinations, constituting a classic SSRF.

descriptions.value:
The html_to_markdown expansion module in MISP Modules contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its is_safe_url() URL validation function. The BLOCKED_RANGES list used to reject unsafe destination addresses was incomplete, omitting several critical IP address ranges. Specifically, the following ranges were not blocked: 0.0.0.0/8 (unspecified, which routes to loopback on Linux), 100.64.0.0/10 (carrier-grade NAT per RFC 6598), ::/128 (IPv6 unspecified), fc00::/7 (IPv6 Unique Local Addresses), and fe80::/10 (IPv6 link-local). The existing list only covered IPv4 loopback (127.0.0.0/8), RFC 1918 private ranges, IPv4 link-local (169.254.0.0/16), and IPv6 loopback (::1/128).

An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify MISP attributes that trigger the html_to_markdown expansion module could supply URLs pointing to these unblocked internal address ranges. Because the module fetches the URL server-side to convert HTML content to Markdown, the request is made from the MISP server's network context. This allows an attacker to probe and read responses from internal services, carrier-grade NAT infrastructure, or link-local endpoints that would otherwise be unreachable from external networks. IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms (e.g., [::ffff:0.0.0.0]) also bypassed the existing checks.

The security impact is primarily confidentiality: an attacker can read data served by internal services reachable from the MISP server. The MISP instance itself is not compromised, but it is abused as a proxy to access otherwise restricted network resources.

descriptions.value: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.1.0 through 5.6.2, the Configuration REST API v2 (org.eclipse.kura.rest.configuration.provider) does not restrict access to the configuration of the UserAdmin persistence component to identities holding the kura.admin permission. ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [sync] Only use a valid colour for remote tags in the

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [sync] Only use a valid colour for remote tags in the
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix introduces strict validation of the tag colour value before it is rendered into a CSS style attribute. Only values matching a valid six-digit hexadecimal colour pattern (e.g. #aabbcc) are accepted; any other value is replaced with a safe default (#ffffff). This prevents arbitrary CSS from being injected through the colour field, aligning the remote tag handling with the validation already applied to local tags.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48, 27 commits after fix); the exact first affected version is not stated in the patch.
PR:L assumes that creating or modifying a tag on a linked MISP server requires only low-level user privileges; the exact permission model was not verified from the patch.
SC:L assumes CSS injection could enable limited client-side information disclosure (e.g., via CSS selectors or layout manipulation); full XSS or data exfiltration is not evidenced.
CAPEC-66 is the closest available mapping; no CAPEC specifically models CSS injection via trusted inter-instance data, so this mapping carries uncertainty.
The commit message states the issue was found during internal review and not externally reported; no external finder or reporter is credited.
The Co-Authored-By line references an AI tool (Claude Opus 5.5); it is credited as a tool rather than a human remediation developer.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/View/Servers/preview_event.ctp, a regex check (preg_match against /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i) is added before the tag colour is used. If the colour does not match the hex pattern, it defaults to #ffffff. The validated $colour variable replaces the raw $tag['colour'] in both the background-color style property and the getTextColour() call, eliminating the untrusted value from the CSS context.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N – the attack originates from a remote linked MISP server over the network. AC:L – no race conditions or special timing; simply setting a tag colour suffices. AT:N – no manipulation of the attack target is required. PR:L – the attacker needs low-privilege access (tag creation) on the linked server. UI:A – the victim must actively navigate to the event preview page. VC:N – no direct confidentiality loss on the vulnerable system. VI:N – no integrity impact on the vulnerable system's data. VA:N – no availability impact. SC:L – CSS injection may allow limited information disclosure on the client (e.g., reading page structure via CSS selectors or side channels). SI:L – the attacker can modify the visual presentation of the preview page (UI manipulation, overlay, spoofing). SA:N – no security authority impact.

capecRationale.rationale: The attack exploits the inherent trust between linked MISP instances. The local instance accepts and renders data (tag colours) from a remote linked server without sufficient validation, assuming the data is well-formed. The attacker leverages this trusted relationship to inject CSS. This is the closest CAPEC; no CAPEC specifically models CSS injection via trusted data sources, so CAPEC-66 is the best available match.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The tag colour value is not neutralized for the CSS context in which it is placed. HTML entity encoding (h()) does not sanitize CSS metacharacters such as semicolons, colons, or function calls, allowing CSS injection. CWE-74 is the most precise parent weakness covering injection into a downstream component (CSS) without a more specific child CWE for CSS injection.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a CSS injection vulnerability in the remote event preview feature. When a user previews an event from a linked MISP server, the colour value associated with each remote tag is written directly into an inline CSS style attribute without sufficient validation. Although HTML entity encoding is applied, the value is interpreted as CSS within the style attribute, allowing a malicious or compromised linked server to inject arbitrary CSS declarations.

An attacker with the ability to create or modify tags on a linked MISP instance can craft a tag colour value containing CSS injection payloads. When a user on the local instance views the event preview, the injected CSS is rendered, potentially allowing UI manipulation, visual spoofing, or limited information disclosure through CSS-based techniques.

Preconditions:

- A linked MISP server relationship exists between the victim instance and the attacker-controlled instance.

- The attacker can create or modify tags on the linked server.

- A victim user views the remote event preview page.

Affected: <2.5.48.

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [proposals] Apply the attribute ACL rules to proposals

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [proposals] Apply the attribute ACL rules to proposals
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix enforces the distribution level constraint in the sharing group access check, requiring distribution level 4 (All communities) for the sharing group test to apply. Additionally, the owning organisation is now explicitly granted access to proposals on its own attributes regardless of distribution level, correcting the over-restrictive behavior.
assumptions: The CAPEC mapping (CAPEC-2, Parameter Tampering) is the closest available match but is uncertain; the vulnerability is more accurately a missing authorization check (incomplete ACL evaluation) rather than active parameter manipulation by the attacker.
The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag v2.5.48 and the commit position (35 commits after the fix); exact version boundaries are not explicitly stated in the patch metadata.

The second aspect of the vulnerability (owner organisation denied access to its own proposals) is primarily a functional/availability defect rather than a security vulnerability, but is included as part of the same fix and the same root cause (incomplete ACL logic).
CVSS PR:L assumes the attacker must be an authenticated MISP user with membership in a relevant sharing group; no evidence supports unauthenticated access.
The Co-Authored-By line credits an AI assistant (Claude Opus 5.5) as a remediation developer; this is recorded as-is from the commit metadata.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In the shadow attribute model's condition builder, the sharing group check for both objects and attributes now includes an AND condition requiring distribution = 4 alongside the sharing_group_id IN check. The attribute distribution condition was changed from a simple sharing_group_id IN clause to a compound AND condition with distribution = 4. A new OR condition (Event.org_id matching the user's org_id) was added to grant the owning organisation access to proposals on its own attributes.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a network-accessible web application. AC:L: The user only needs to be a member of a sharing group; no special conditions or race conditions are required. AT:N: No active attack requirements beyond normal API usage. PR:L: The attacker must be an authenticated user with membership in a relevant sharing group. UI:N: No user interaction is required; the check is server-side. VC:H: The user can view proposals (proposed attribute changes) that should be restricted by distribution level, disclosing sensitive information about proposed changes. VI:N: No integrity impact; the user cannot modify proposals. VA:N: No availability impact. SC/SI/SA:N: No impact on subsequent components.

capecRationale.rationale: The user's sharing group membership (a parameter of their identity/session) was leveraged by the flawed authorization logic to grant access to proposals without the required distribution level check. This is the closest available CAPEC pattern; the user is not actively tampering with parameters, but the system improperly treats group membership as a sufficient access parameter without enforcing the additional distribution constraint. The mapping is uncertain because the vulnerability is more accurately a missing authorization check than active parameter manipulation.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The authorization check for proposal visibility was missing the distribution level constraint. The system evaluated sharing group membership as sufficient for access without also requiring the distribution level to be 4 (All communities), resulting in an incomplete authorization check that allowed access to proposals on more restrictively distributed attributes.

solutions.value: The fix enforces the distribution level constraint in the sharing group access check, requiring distribution level 4 (All communities) for the sharing group test to apply. Additionally, the owning organisation is now explicitly granted access to proposals on its own attributes regardless of distribution level, correcting the over-restrictive behavior.

descriptions.value: An IPv6 FlowSpec validation bypass in the CZ.NIC BIRD Internet Routing Daemon allows an established BGP peer to inject FlowSpec rules matching destinations outside the address space authorized by the unicast-route validation procedure. Given a suitable unicast route from the peer, the rule can pass validation and, where export policy permits, be propagated to downstream peers. Downstream enforcement may cause unauthorized traffic filtering or redirection.

cna.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.0.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow has a heap buffer overflow and stale-heap disclosure in _tiffWriteProc when saving compressed TIFF data through libtiff to a target without a usable fileno(), such as BytesIO. The callback sizes its allocation from the prior buffer size instead of the current write position, allowing an attacker-controlled out-of-line TIFF tag or retained ICC profile to be copied beyond the allocation after libtiff seeks forward. This overflow can crash the process and may allow code execution. File paths and targets with real file descriptors are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

descriptions.value: vault-java-driver, a Java client for HashiCorp Vault, parses Vault's JSON responses with a vendored minimal-json parser that has no nesting depth limit. cna.title: Apache Kafka: Unauthorized principal can read arbitrary broker files via IncrementalAlterConfigs

credits.value: Arthur Chan <arthur.chan@adalogics.com>, Ada Logics and Anthropic Research
OpenAI Codex Security - Amy Burnett and Khai Tran

descriptions.value:
An authenticated Kafka principal with no authorization grants (not even ALTER_CONFIGS) can make a broker read a file or an environment variable from the broker host and return its contents. An IncrementalAlterConfigs (or AlterConfigs) request targeting a BROKER resource reaches the broker's configuration validation before any authorization check is applied to that path. Validation resolves configuration variables such as ${file:/path:key} or ${env:VAR} using a ConfigProvider named in the request, and this resolution bypasses the org.apache.kafka.automatic.config.providers allowlist that was added as the mitigation for CVE-2024-31141. An arbitrary ConfigProvider (for example FileConfigProvider or EnvVarConfigProvider) is therefore instantiated and the referenced file or environment variable is read, and a type-validation error returns the resolved content to the caller.


Impact:

On a cluster with an authorizer enabled, an authenticated principal with no authorization grants can read the contents of files accessible to the broker process, and the broker's environment variables, exposing credentials, keystores, or other secrets, defeating the CVE-2024-31141 allowlist. The read is bounded by the broker process's file permissions. The brokers and the cluster remain available; the issue is disclosure of file and environment- variable contents. Clusters with no authorizer configured are not affected in practice, because every principal already holds ALTER_CONFIGS there.


Mitigation:

Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. As defense in depth, run brokers under a least-privileged operating-system account so that sensitive files are not readable by the broker process.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: broker configuration changes are authorized (ALTER_CONFIGS on the cluster) before the configuration is validated, and configuration- variable resolution enforces the config-providers allowlist.

An authenticated Kafka principal with no authorization grants (not even ALTER_CONFIGS) can make a broker read a file or an environment variable from the broker host and return its contents. An IncrementalAlterConfigs (or AlterConfigs) request targeting a BROKER resource reaches the broker's configuration validation before any authorization check is applied to that path. credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Nicholas Pettas for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-10-20) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to eliminate privileged .forceput operations in the .charkeys procedure to enforce -dSAFER sandbox boundaries: upgrade to the fixed Ghostscript builds, which replace .forceput invocations with standard put operations in the /.charkeys procedure in Resource/Init/gs_ttf.ps, closing all 2 injection vectors (crafted PostScript document, malicious TrueType font processing). Until patched, this is a concern on Ghostscript on Linux (RHEL 8) processing untrusted input, such as print or document-conversion services, so Restrict or halt processing of untrusted PostScript documents and TrueType font inputs across document-conversion and printing services that invoke Ghostscript. As a compensating measure, Use auditd to log unauthorized file access attempts and unexpected execve syscalls spawned by the Ghostscript process, Run SELinux in enforcing mode to confine the Ghostscript process to a restricted domain, Use Linux mount and PID namespaces to restrict filesystem and process visibility for Ghostscript execution, Deploy an EDR agent to detect and terminate unexpected shell or child process spawns from Ghostscript, and Use Falco or eBPF runtime security to detect anomalous child process execution and unauthorized file reads. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying privileged .forceput sandbox bypass — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1002 Audit Subsystem (auditd) (medium)

This prevents the redaction check from being bypassed and stops the endpoints from returning entire configuration branches containing sensitive values.
assumptions: The exact privilege level required to access the server settings endpoints (admin vs. any authenticated user) is not stated in the patch; PR:L is assumed as the most conservative defensible value.

The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48 with 11 commits after fix); the exact last affected version and first fixed version are not explicitly confirmed.
CAPEC-124 (Parameter Tampering) is the closest available attack pattern; no CAPEC specifically models configuration-tree branch traversal, so the mapping is approximate.
The patch does not indicate whether unauthenticated access is possible; authentication is assumed based on the nature of server settings endpoints in MISP.
The Co-Authored-By line references an AI tool (Claude Opus 5); it is listed as a tool credit rather than a human remediation developer.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Server.php, the getSettingData() method previously checked only for the presence of a 'level' key before returning the setting. The patch adds a guard clause: if the resolved setting is an array (i.e., a branch/sub-tree) or lacks the 'level' key, the function immediately returns false. The existing logic for setting the name and resolving options is then applied only to confirmed leaf settings. This ensures callers that assumed a single-setting result never receive a multi-key branch.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a network-accessible web application. AC:L: The attack requires only substituting a branch name for a leaf setting name in an existing API call; no race conditions or complex timing are needed. AT:N: No manipulation of the target environment is required. PR:L: The attacker needs an authenticated account with access to the server settings endpoints; the exact privilege level (admin vs. regular user) is not confirmed in the patch, so Low is assumed. UI:N: No victim interaction is required. VC:H: Sensitive secrets (security salt, Redis passwords, plugin API keys) are fully disclosed. VI:N, VA:N: No integrity or availability impact is evidenced. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N: No impact on subsequent components is indicated.

capecRationale.rationale: The attacker manipulates the setting name parameter supplied to the settings lookup endpoint, substituting a branch name (e.g., 'Security') for a leaf setting name. This causes the application to return a broader data set than intended. CAPEC-124 is the closest match because the core technique is altering a request parameter to change the application's response scope. The mapping is approximate because the parameter is not a traditional HTTP parameter but an application-level setting identifier; no CAPEC specifically covers configuration-tree traversal.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The settings endpoint returned sensitive configuration values (security salt, Redis passwords, plugin API keys) to a caller who requested a branch name, bypassing the intended redaction mechanism. The data was exposed to an actor who should not have had access to those specific values.

The redaction check, which serves as an authorization control for sensitive setting values, was effectively bypassed because branch nodes do not carry a redacted flag. The system failed to enforce the intended access restriction on sensitive configuration data.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a vulnerability in its server settings lookup mechanism that allows an authenticated user to retrieve sensitive configuration data that should have been redacted.

The settings lookup function resolves a dotted setting name to a node in the configuration tree. When a branch name (such as Security, MISP, or Plugin) is supplied instead of a specific leaf setting, the function returns the entire sub-tree. Because a branch node does not carry a redaction flag, the redaction check in the settings retrieval endpoint is bypassed, and the full branch contents are returned to the caller. This exposes sensitive values including the security salt, Redis connection passwords, and plugin API keys.

A second endpoint that edits server settings similarly reads the entire configuration store when a branch name is resolved, returning all settings to the caller.

The impact is disclosure of sensitive server configuration secrets to any user who can access the server settings endpoints.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

cna.title: webpack-dev-server vulnerable to cross-origin WebSocket access via proxied upgrades

descriptions.value: webpack-dev-server is a development server that provides live reloading for webpack projects. In versions before 5.2.7 and in version 6.0.0, when a proxy entry is configured to forward WebSockets, the server forwards non-HMR WebSocket upgrade requests to the proxy target without validating the Host or Origin headers, so the allowedHosts protection does not apply to those proxied upgrades. A malicious web page visited by a developer can open a cross-origin WebSocket through the dev server and read from and write to the proxied backend, even when the server is bound to loopback. The issue is fixed in webpack-dev-server 5.2.7 and 6.1.0, where proxied WebSocket upgrades pass the same Host and Origin validation as the HMR WebSocket, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, omit WebSocket forwarding from proxy entries that do not need it and scope the proxy to specific paths.

cna.title: Vite: First 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting is exposed by `?vite-wasm-instance`

descriptions.value: Vite is a frontend tooling framework for JavaScript. From 8.2.0 until 8.2.4 and 8.3.3, the first 4 bytes of files outside of server.fs setting can be returned to the browser by a request containing ?vite-wasm-instance. Requests containing the ?vite-wasm-instance query are handled by the internal Wasm plugin's load hook. The hook removes the query and reads the resulting path directly from disk, but the server.fs checks were not applied. After reading the file, Vite attempts to parse it as WebAssembly. When that parse fails, Node and deno throws an error that contains the first 4 bytes of the file. This vulnerability is fixed in 8.2.4 and 8.3.3.

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow can double free image memory when ImagingScaleAffine encounters a selective allocation failure. The affected fast path handles Transform.EXTENT or pure scale-and-translate Transform.AFFINE operations with the default NEAREST resampling. The output image allocation must succeed while the additional per-column lookup allocation fails, after which the error path deletes image storage that later cleanup releases again. An attacker who can drive such a large Image.transform() operation under memory pressure may trigger the failure. This can crash the process and may corrupt memory. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: libmng through 2.0.3 Heap Buffer Overflow via ORDR Chunk Reader mng_read_ordr

descriptions.value:
Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in hackney_http_connect in benoitc hackney allows HTTP Request Splitting via the value a proxy_auth_fun callback returns. After a 407 response from an HTTP CONNECT proxy, hackney_http_connect:handle_proxy_auth/11 calls the caller's proxy_auth_fun with the status code and the response headers and writes the returned binary into the Proxy-Authorization line of the CONNECT retry without checking it. A CR, LF or NUL byte in that value adds header lines to the request sent to the proxy.

The value is attacker-influenced when the callback derives it from untrusted data, for example from the proxy's challenge headers. Other caller-supplied values on the CONNECT path, such as the target host and the request headers, were already checked for control bytes.

This issue affects hackney: from 2.0.0 before 4.9.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Challenge. hackney_http_connect:do_handshake_with_auth/9 in src/hackney_http_connect.erl sends the CONNECT request to the proxy. When the proxy answers 407 and the proxy_auth_fun option is set, it hands the status code and the parsed response headers to hackney_http_connect:handle_proxy_auth/11.

2. Callback result. handle_proxy_auth/11 calls the caller's proxy_auth_fun with those two values. On {ok, AuthHeader} it removes any existing Proxy-Authorization header and appends the binary <<"Proxy-Authorization: ", AuthHeader/binary>> to the header list, then retries the handshake with it.

3. Splitting. The header list is joined with CRLF into the CONNECT request. A CR, LF or NUL byte inside AuthHeader therefore ends the Proxy-Authorization line early and the rest is sent as further header lines. The target host and the request headers go through control-byte checks on this path; the callback result did not. The fix applies the same has_ctl_bytes/1 check to it and returns {error, {proxy_auth_error, invalid_header}}.

cna.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in FlashPix (FPX) JPEG decoding leads to code execution

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's FlashPix JPEG-tile decoder can write decoded scanlines beyond the allocated tile buffer. FlashPix (FPX) JPEG decoding selects raw mode LA with two bytes per pixel, while an unrecognized JPEG mode can be decoded as JCS_UNKNOWN with four components, causing ImagingJpegDecode to write four-component scanlines into the two-byte tile buffer. An attacker can supply a crafted OLE2 FlashPix file to an application with the optional olefile dependency installed that opens or thumbnails untrusted input. This can corrupt heap memory and may allow arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

descriptions.value: Vite is a frontend tooling framework for JavaScript. Prior to 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4, and 8.3.3, import analysis can record a root-relative browser URL in safeModulePaths instead of the cleaned resolved module identifier. On a network-accessible, non-Windows development server, an imported project file whose URL matches an absolute host path can authorize a later raw-filesystem request for that host file, provided server.fs.deny does not block it. The request can disclose the matching file outside the project root, but it does not allow arbitrary path traversal because the host path must correspond to a project-relative URL authorized by the application graph. This issue is fixed in versions 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4, and 8.3.3.
