cna.title: Pillow: Argument Injection in Ghostscript call, potentially leading into RCE

descriptions.description: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
CWE-88: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.6.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow is vulnerable to argument injection when invoking Ghostscript for EPS input. EpsImagePlugin.Ghostscript passes a caller-controlled input filename after -f without converting it to a safe absolute path, so a name beginning with a hyphen can be interpreted as a Ghostscript option. An attacker who controls the filename can inject Ghostscript arguments. Arbitrary command execution specifically requires a leading @ argument-file filename and control of the referenced text file containing additional Ghostscript arguments; the reported chain reproduces with the default -dSAFER invocation. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Pillow: P;2L and P;4L decoders may read 1 to 3 bytes past the passed buffer size

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's P;2L and P;4L raw decoders can read past the end of an input buffer. ImagingRawDecode calculates a packed-pixel row size, while the unpackers read separately padded bit planes. A caller can supply a buffer and image dimensions whose accepted size is smaller than the unpacker's actual footprint. This can disclose up to three adjacent heap bytes in output pixels or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: filelock: ReadWriteLock on Windows acts on SQLite side files another local user places beside its database

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.20.4 until 4.2.1, ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock on Windows use _connect to attach SQLite to the lock database by pathname, allowing another local account that can create adjacent names to place a database-wal or database-journal side file before acquisition. An undeletable WAL file makes each read or write acquisition fail immediately with sqlite3.OperationalError regardless of timeout. Separately, when the database contains at least one table, a hot journal that grants the lock account modify rights can cause SQLite recovery to delete a file named by that journal only when the lock account has permission to delete the target. The issue requires a directory writable by another account, such as a shared Windows temporary directory, and does not affect private directories. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.
This issue was addressed with improved input validation. This issue is fixed in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2. An app may be able to access sensitive user data.

cna.title: @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via absolute-form request targets

descriptions.value: @fastify/express is a Fastify plugin that runs Express middleware inside Fastify. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.8, when Fastify runs with the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option enabled, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware against a URL whose duplicate-slash normalization has also collapsed the separator after an absolute-form request target's scheme, so Fastify's router resolves the request to the scoped path and runs the handler while the Express layer no longer sees that path. As a result, a request using an absolute-form target can reach a handler on a scoped route such as an admin path while the middleware for authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is skipped. An unauthenticated attacker needs only the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option to be enabled. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.9, and users should upgrade to 4.0.9 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request, or leave ignoreDuplicateSlashes at its default.

cna.title: filelock: On Windows an oplock on a soft lock's marker holds SoftFileLock.acquire() past its timeout and blocks the stale break

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.22.0 until 4.2.1, soft lock classes on Windows read an existing marker with _read_lock_file and remove a stale marker through break_lock_file using pathname operations that wait for an oplock break. Another local account with read access to an unheld marker can keep a Level 1 or batch oplock unanswered, causing SoftFileLock.acquire and related async or fallback locks to wait beyond timeout, blocking=False, and cancel_check. A stale marker under the oplock cannot be broken, but mutual exclusion remains intact and no file other than the marker is accessed. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The event deletion routine was extended to cascade-remove all associated child records that were previously left behind. Specifically, the fix ensures that event report tags, event graph rows, shadow attribute correlation rows (on both event_id and 1_event_id foreign keys), fuzzy ssdeep chunks, and attachment scan results are all purged within the same transaction as the parent event deletion, eliminating the orphaned-data condition.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48 with 33 commits after fix); the exact fixed release version is not specified in the patch.

The CAPEC-126 mapping is the closest available match; the vulnerability is fundamentally an incomplete cleanup defect rather than a classic state-transition exploit, so the mapping carries uncertainty.

The confidentiality impact is assessed as None because the patch does not demonstrate that orphaned records are accessible to unauthorized users; the primary concern is data integrity and retention policy.
The commit message states the issue was 'found during the internal review, not externally reported,' so no external finder or reporter is credited.
The CVSS assumes the orphaned data is not directly queryable by other users through existing MISP endpoints; if such access paths exist, the confidentiality impact could be higher.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Event.php, the quickDelete method was modified to: (1) add event_graph and shadow_attribute_correlations (both event_id and 1_event_id) to the relations array used for raw DELETE statements; (2) before executing the raw deletes, query for the IDs of event reports and for attribute/shadow-attribute IDs of type 'attachment' or 'malware-sample'; (3) delete EventReportTag rows matching those report IDs; (4) delete AttachmentScan rows matching those attribute IDs; (5) invoke FuzzyCorrelateSsdeep::purge() to remove ssdeep chunks for the event. All operations occur within the existing database transaction.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: The vulnerability is in a web-based application (AV:N) and requires a straightforward authenticated action (AC:L, AT:N). Deleting events requires elevated privileges (PR:H). No user interaction is needed (UI:N). The primary impact is on the integrity of the vulnerable system's data store: orphaned records persist that should have been removed (VI:L). There is no direct confidentiality impact on the vulnerable system itself because the data was already accessible to the deleting user, and no evidence shows the orphans are exposed to other users (VC:N). No availability impact is demonstrated (VA:N). No impact on subsequent systems (SC:N, SI:N, SA:N).

capecRationale.rationale: The event object transitions to a 'deleted' state, but related child objects (report tags, correlations, scan results, ssdeep chunks) do not follow the expected state transition and remain in an active/persisted state. An attacker with delete privileges could exploit this by creating events with sensitive associated data, deleting the event, and then attempting to access the orphaned records through other application endpoints. This is the closest CAPEC to the observed incomplete state propagation; the mapping is uncertain because the primary issue is a maintenance/cleanup defect rather than a directly exploitable state machine flaw.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The event deletion logic failed to remove all associated child records (report tags, graphs, correlations, ssdeep chunks, scan results), leaving them as orphans in the database. This is a textbook incomplete cleanup of related resources when a parent object is destroyed.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a data integrity flaw in its event deletion logic. When a user deletes an event, several associated records are not removed from the database, leaving them as orphaned entries. The affected record types include event report tags, event graph entries, proposal (shadow attribute) correlations, fuzzy ssdeep correlation chunks, and attachment scan results.

These orphaned records may contain sensitive threat intelligence data such as correlation mappings, scan results, and report metadata that should have been removed along with the parent event. Their persistence beyond the intended deletion lifecycle creates a risk of unintended data retention and potential information exposure if the records are reachable through other application queries or administrative interfaces.

Preconditions:

- An authenticated user with sufficient privileges to delete events in MISP.

- The event must have associated reports, graphs, correlations, ssdeep chunks, or attachment scan results.

Impact:

- Residual sensitive data persists in the database after the parent event is deleted.

- Accumulation of orphaned records over time may contribute to storage bloat.

- Orphaned records may be inadvertently exposed through other data-access paths that do not validate the existence of the parent event.

Affected versions: <2.5.48

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to ensure the SSO_AUTH re-authentication note is cleared from the authentication session whenever a flow transition strips the authenticated user: upgrade to Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.6.8 (or the fixed Rhbk/Keycloak Rhel/Keycloak Services builds), which clears the lingering SSO_AUTH re-authentication note from the authentication session during login flow transitions such as registration or credential reset, closing all 2 injection vectors (transition to credential reset flow, transition to registration flow). Until patched, this is a concern on Keycloak deployments with the Organization feature enabled and users holding credentials in multiple organizations, so Disable the Organization feature or ensure users cannot hold memberships across multiple organizations. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying stale authentication state flag defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Organization identity-first login flow of the Keycloak authentication server. Keycloak is an open-source identity and access management solution used to secure modern applications and services. The issue occurs when an attacker who belongs to multiple organizations initiates a login and then switches to a registration or password reset path. During this process, a flag indicating a successful login is not properly cleared when the user is removed from the session. An attacker can then provide a victim's username, and the system incorrectly treats the stale flag as proof of the victim's identity. This allows the attacker to bypass authentication and gain full access to the victim's account and connected applications.

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [settings] Module settings keep the flags the module
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix ensures that the redacted and cli_only flags declared by a module in its own setting definition are preserved when the server rebuilds the setting for API exposure. By carrying these flags through to the final setting object, the existing enforcement logic (which checks these flags before serving values or accepting edits) now correctly applies to module-supplied settings, preventing disclosure of redacted values and blocking API-based modification of CLI-only settings.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (fix is 10 commits after v2.5.48); the exact fixed release version is not stated in the patch metadata.
PR:L assumes that reading server settings requires an authenticated MISP user with appropriate role permissions; the patch does not specify the exact permission level required.

The CAPEC-126 mapping is the closest available pattern for the information-disclosure aspect; the authorization-bypass aspect (cli_only) does not have a precise CAPEC match and is subsumed under the same mapping.
VC:L assumes the exposed data is limited to module-specific API keys rather than system-wide credentials; the actual sensitivity depends on which modules are installed.

The commit message references a separate issue (branch read) reported by Jeroen Pinoy; this vulnerability was discovered as a side effect of fixing that issue, so Jeroen Pinoy is not credited as a finder of this specific vulnerability.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Server.php, within the readModuleSettings() method, a loop was added after the setting fields are populated that iterates over the strings 'redacted' and 'cli_only'. For each flag, if the module's own result array contains a truthy value for that key, the flag is set to true on the rebuilt $setting object before it is stored in $serverSettings. This is a 6-line addition that preserves the module-declared guard flags that were previously discarded during the setting reconstruction.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a web application accessible over the network. AC:L: No special race conditions or complex setup are needed; a standard API call to the settings endpoint triggers the issue. AT:N: No manipulation of the attack target is required. PR:L: The attacker needs an authenticated MISP account with permission to view server settings. UI:N: No user interaction is required. VC:L: Sensitive module API keys are exposed, but the scope is limited to settings of modules that declare the redacted flag. VI:N: No direct integrity impact on the vulnerable component's data beyond the VA impact. VA:L: CLI-only settings can be modified via the API, representing a limited integrity impact on the vulnerable component's configuration. SC/SI/SA:N: No evidence of impact on other components or systems.

capecRationale.rationale: The primary impact is that sensitive data (module API keys marked as redacted) is discoverable via standard API endpoints because the redaction flag was not enforced. An authenticated user querying server settings can obtain credentials that the module author intended to keep hidden. This is the closest CAPEC to the information-disclosure aspect of the vulnerability. The secondary aspect (CLI-only settings editable via API) is an authorization bypass that does not map cleanly to a single CAPEC; CAPEC-126 is selected as the best available match for the overall pattern of accessing data that should be restricted.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The redacted flag, which instructs the server to mask a setting's value (e.g., an API key), was dropped during setting reconstruction. This caused the sensitive value to be served in plaintext via API endpoints to any authenticated user, constituting an information exposure.

The cli_only flag, which restricts a setting to command-line modification only, was dropped during setting reconstruction. This allowed the setting to be modified via the web API without the intended authorization restriction, effectively bypassing the access control the module author specified.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a vulnerability in the handling of module plugin settings. When the server rebuilds module-supplied settings for API consumption, it drops the redacted and cli_only flags that a module declares in its own configuration metadata.

As a result:

- A module that marks a setting (such as an API key) as redacted still has its value returned in full by the servers/getSetting and servers/serverSettingsEdit endpoints, exposing sensitive credentials to any authenticated user who can read server settings.

- A module that marks a setting as cli_only (intended to be editable only via the command-line interface) can still be modified through the web API, bypassing the intended access restriction.

An authenticated user with access to server settings can therefore read sensitive module credentials and modify settings that the module author intended to restrict to CLI-only access.

Affected: <2.5.48

Submit #1009600 | radareorg radare2 up to 6.2.2 OS Command Injection

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was detected in radareorg radare2 6.2.0/6.2.2. This issue affects the function r_core_cmd_str_pipe in the library libr/core/rtr_http.inc.c of the component HTTP Sandbox Policy Handler. Performing a manipulation results in protection mechanism failure. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The attack is considered to have high complexity. The exploitability is assessed as difficult. Upgrading to version 6.2.4 is capable of addressing this issue. The patch is named 18fd12efa98a7d1977de7bdd379d8a848777b90f. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The pre-requisite of the vulnerability is reflected by the CVSS vector. One of the project maintainers explains: "There is a real sandbox configuration issue here, but the report overstates it. The HTTP server defaults to http.sandbox=true, so commands received through /cmd temporarily enable cfg.sandbox. However, cfg.sandbox.grain defaults to all, which means all sandbox capabilities - including exec - remain allowed. Therefore enabling the HTTP sandbox alone does NOT prevent commands from spawning processes. This only matters when the HTTP command endpoint is reachable by someone you do not trust. It is not a remote vulnerability by default: the HTTP server must first be started and exposed to the attacker."

cna.title: Pillow: Infinite loop in MIC n_frames when the embedded TIFF

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 7.2.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow can enter an infinite loop while determining the frame count of a MIC image. MicImageFile inherits TIFF frame traversal, but MicImageFile.tell reports the OLE stream index and its seek() resets TIFF frame state, so an embedded TIFF with at least three IFDs never advances. When an application with olefile installed reads n_frames or saves all frames from a crafted MIC file, the non-advancing traversal can hold a worker at full CPU indefinitely. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Semih Doğan for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the login-failure storage component of Keycloak, the identity and access management solution. This issue specifically affects deployments using MySQL or MariaDB databases in a multi-node configuration. When multiple failed login attempts occur simultaneously for the same account, a synchronization error can cause the system to enter a repetitive loop that locks the user's record in the database. This results in legitimate login attempts for that user being blocked and failing with an error. Furthermore, because some failures are not correctly recorded during this loop, the system's brute-force protection may not accurately count all failed attempts.

cna.title: Resource exhaustion from unreleased AR and RPC session on RPC requests with incorrect endianness

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.3 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.3 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.3 does not release the Application Relationship (AR) and the RPC session when an RPC request is rejected because its data representation has incorrect endianness. The session and its AR remain allocated, so repeated requests exhaust the available sessions. Once they are exhausted the device no longer answers new RPC requests, including Connect, until it is restarted. A remote unauthenticated attacker can use this to cause a denial of service.

descriptions.value: The extension hides the correct answer to each CAPTCHA inside the image data of the CAPTCHA itself. Anyone who can request a CAPTCHA image can read the answer from it and submit it, so automated clients can pass the challenge. descriptions.value: The Bootstrap Shortcodes plugin for WordPress before 3.4.6 is vulnerable to stored XSS via the id attribute of the [bs_tcontent] shortcode. The bs_tcontent() shortcode handler in inc/bs_tabs.php emits the id attribute value into an unquoted HTML attribute. esc_attr() is applied, but it does not encode space characters, so a space in the supplied value terminates the attribute and any following text is parsed as additional HTML attributes, including JavaScript event handlers. This allows authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to inject arbitrary web script that executes in the browser of any user who views the page and interacts with the injected element.

cna.title: Vvveb: Path Traversal in nextRestore() and nextBackup()

descriptions.value: Vvveb is a powerful and easy to use CMS with page builder to build websites, blogs or ecommerce stores. In versions 1.0.8.6 and prior, the nextRestore() and nextBackup() functions in the backup controller accept a file GET parameter and concatenate it directly to DIR_BACKUP without calling sanitizeFileName(). This allows an authenticated administrator to read arbitrary files on the server (via nextRestore) and write SQL dump content to arbitrary locations (via nextBackup). This is inconsistent with the sibling functions restore(), delete(), and download() which all correctly call sanitizeFileName() first. This issue has been patched via commit aa29cb0.

cna.title: launch-editor: Editor CLI flag misinterpretation causing arbitrary command execution for some editors

descriptions.value: launch-editor allows users to open files with line numbers in editor from Node.js. Prior to 2.14.2, when an attacker can create a filesystem entry beginning with plus or minus in the working directory, an affected editor is selected, and the path can remain relative or is converted to a relative WSL path, launchEditor forwards the path without forcing it to be interpreted as a positional filename. Editor option parsing then treats the attacker-controlled filename as a command-line flag, which can cause unintended file overwrite or arbitrary command execution by the selected editor. The affected editors are Vim and gVim, MacVim, Emacs and Emacsclient, and Notepad++ when a plugin exposes dangerous operations; WSL path conversion keeps Vite and newer middleware callers exposed. This issue is fixed in version 2.14.2.

cna.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in ImagingJpegDecode

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. ImagingJpegDecode does not verify libjpeg's actual output width and component count after scaling is requested, and an 8-bit lossless SOF3 JPEG decoded by a build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x can ignore the requested downscaling geometry. An attacker can supply such a JPEG to an application that uses draft() or thumbnail() to request downscaling. This can corrupt heap memory, crash the process, or potentially allow code execution. Older libjpeg-turbo 2.x and IJG builds reject the SOF3 input. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Imager::File::GIF versions before 1.006 for Perl allow out-of-bounds reads when consolidating GIF images

solutions.value: Upgrade to Imager-File-GIF 1.006 or later, or to Imager 1.040 or later if the bundled copy is in use.

workarounds.value: Disable the gif_consolidate read option when processing untrusted GIF images.

descriptions.value:
Imager::File::GIF versions before 1.006 for Perl allow out-of-bounds reads when consolidating GIF images.

With `gif_consolidate => 1`, palette indices from the image are used without checking the colour table's bounds. The i_readgif_low routine reads beyond the heap allocation and copies the bytes into output pixels. The default GIF reader is not affected.

The same code ships bundled in the Imager distribution.

An attacker supplying a crafted GIF can disclose adjacent heap memory through the decoded output and may crash the process.

cna.title: Pillow tiled-TIFF decoder reads past tile buffer in copy4 (Unpack.c:1290)

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 8.2.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow's tiled-TIFF decoder can read past the tile buffer while copying four-byte pixels. In _decodeTile, libtiff can return a tile allocation smaller than the required row stride multiplied by the tile length, and Pillow's stride-and-copy loop walks beyond that allocation. An attacker can supply a crafted tiled TIFF to an application that loads it. This can expose adjacent heap data in pixels or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Pillow: Quadratic GIF comment concatenation allows DoS in Image.open()

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.4.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow performs quadratic copying while parsing GIF comments. GifImageFile._seek() repeatedly appends immutable bytes for comment sub-blocks and multiple comment extensions, and frame zero is parsed during Image.open(). An attacker can submit a small-dimension GIF containing many comment extensions to any application that opens the file. This can consume excessive CPU and deny service before the application can inspect the image. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Pillow: Out-of-bounds access in _imagingmorph on a zero-width image

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's ImageMorph.MorphOp.apply() can access memory before a row buffer for a zero-width image. PPM and PGM input can create an image with width zero, and the native morphology routine indexes outrow[width - 1] without rejecting that geometry. An attacker can supply such an image to an application that applies a morphology operation. This can crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Rhc: rhc: local privilege escalation via symlink following in rhc-canonical-facts.service

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank D.M Sithum Vihanga for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Disable the rhc-canonical-facts timer to prevent automatic triggering of the vulnerable service:

    systemctl stop rhc-canonical-facts.timer
    systemctl disable rhc-canonical-facts.timer

Note that this will prevent rhc from updating canonical facts automatically. The rhc connect command will still trigger the service manually.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the rhc-canonical-facts.service systemd unit shipped with rhc. The service runs as root and operates on a file inside a directory owned by an unprivileged system user without verifying that the file is not a symbolic link. A local attacker who has already compromised the privileged yggdrasil system service account can exploit this to gain ownership of arbitrary files, leading to privilege escalation to root.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

versions.version: Leptonica 1.87.0 (commit 13275a2), in builds with JPEG 2000 support enabled via HAVE_LIBJP2K / OpenJPEG.

solutions.value: The manufacturer has confirmed the fix in the jp2kio.c file in the master branch of the official Leptonica repository. It is recommended that you apply the fix and recompile the library.

supportingMedia.value: The manufacturer has confirmed the fix in the jp2kio.c file in the master branch of the official Leptonica repository. It is recommended that you apply the fix and recompile the library.

descriptions.value: Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. When processing a specially crafted JPEG 2000 image, data read from adjacent dynamic memory may be incorporated into the pixels of the decoded image and result in information disclosure to anyone who can access the output.

cna.title: MISP Event Synchronization Exposes Non-Exportable Tags on Remote Instances

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [sync] Filter the tags of every event report pushed to a

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [sync] Filter the tags of every event report pushed to a
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The non-exportable tag filtering is now invoked for each individual event report within the iteration loop, ensuring that restricted tags are removed from every report before it is transmitted to the remote MISP instance. This prevents the leakage of tags that were explicitly marked as non-exportable.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48 with 34 commits after fix), suggesting the fix is included in v2.5.48 and prior versions are affected. No explicit version range is stated in the patch.
PR:L assumes that a non-admin authenticated user with push-to-remote permissions can trigger the sync; if only administrators can initiate sync, PR should be raised to H.
The CAPEC-128 mapping is uncertain; no CAPEC pattern precisely describes a per-item filtering logic error causing data leakage during a legitimate operation.
The security impact is assessed as limited to tag disclosure; the actual sensitivity of 'non-exportable' tags depends on MISP deployment configuration and is not specified in the patch.
The availability impact (null report push causing remote save failure) is considered minor and not reflected in the CVSS vector as the primary concern is information disclosure.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Event.php, the call to __removeNonExportableTags was moved from a single post-loop invocation (which used the last $key value from the foreach) into the else branch of the loop body, so it executes for each non-empty report individually. The post-loop else block that applied the filter to a single report was removed, eliminating both the tag-leakage bug and the null-report push when the last report was empty.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The vulnerability is triggered over the network during MISP-to-MISP synchronization. AC:L: No special conditions are needed beyond a configured sync relationship and an event with multiple reports. AT:N: No attacker interaction is required; the bug triggers on any sync push. PR:L: An authenticated user with permission to push events to a remote server is required. UI:N: No user interaction beyond initiating the sync. VC:L: Non-exportable tags (restricted metadata) are disclosed to the remote instance; the core event data is not exposed. VI:N, VA:N: No integrity or availability impact on the local instance. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N: No impact on the remote instance's confidentiality, integrity, or availability beyond receiving the tags it should not have.

capecRationale.rationale: This is the closest available CAPEC pattern. The vulnerability arises from a code logic error that causes data (non-exportable tags) to be improperly exposed during a legitimate sync operation. The mapping is uncertain because the issue is a logic bug in data filtering rather than a deliberate attacker action; no CAPEC pattern precisely covers 'improper per-item filtering in a loop causing data leakage during a legitimate API operation.'

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: Tags explicitly marked as non-exportable were not filtered from event reports during synchronization, exposing restricted information to the remote MISP instance. The root cause is a logic error (filter applied once instead of per-item), but the security consequence is information disclosure.

solutions.value: The non-exportable tag filtering is now invoked for each individual event report within the iteration loop, ensuring that restricted tags are removed from every report before it is transmitted to the remote MISP instance. This prevents the leakage of tags that were explicitly marked as non-exportable.

supportingMedia.value: The non-exportable tag filtering is now invoked for each individual event report within the iteration loop, ensuring that restricted tags are removed from every report before it is transmitted to the remote MISP instance. descriptions.value:
In MISP, the event synchronization process contained a logic error in the preparation of event reports for remote push. The filtering of non-exportable tags was applied only once after the iteration over all reports, rather than to each individual report.

As a result:

- All reports except the last one in the set were pushed to the remote MISP instance with their non-exportable tags intact, effectively disclosing restricted tag information to the receiving instance.

- When the last report in the set was withheld (empty), a null report was pushed, causing the remote instance to fail saving the event.

This issue affects any MISP instance configured to push events with multiple reports to a remote server via synchronization.

Affected: <2.5.48.

The fix for this is issue is to create a secure configuration.  The 6.6.2.0 release has a best practice entry if the configuration is unsecure.



A secure configuration is to NOT allow creation/recreation of Unauthenticated Endpoints.  If creation/recreation of Unauthenticated Endpoints is required, you should only allow it from trusted networks.

cna.title: filelock ReadWriteLock: SQLite reopens the lock database by name, so a planted symlink or journal file makes the lock user's process overwrite or unlink its own files

descriptions.description: CWE-363: Race Condition Enabling Link Following

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.20.4 until 4.2.1, ReadWriteLock let SQLite reopen the database and side files by name; on POSIX systems an attacker with rename access in a non-sticky parent can swap those names to cause overwrite or unlink operations, while a writable adjacent hot journal is additionally required for attacker-chosen content overwrites. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

cna.title: Pillow: TIFF encoder ColorMap plane-size mismatch causes a heap out-of-bounds read

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's TIFF encoder can read beyond a ColorMap buffer when retained TIFF metadata has a plane size inconsistent with BitsPerSample. A small TIFF can be opened normally and then retain a crafted ColorMap that is reused when the image is saved. An application that re-encodes the attacker's TIFF with libtiff can trigger the out-of-bounds read. This can disclose heap memory in the output or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: filelock: SoftFileLock stale-lock break removes a live lock file on a reused inode number and admits two holders

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.22.0 until 4.2.1, SoftFileLock can break a stale marker after an attacker frees its own marker following the stale read, an honest contender creates a live successor on the reused inode, and the successor's modification time is not newer than the saved observation, causing the live marker to be removed and two holders to be admitted. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

cna.title: Pillow: NULL pointer dereference in Image.merge via an unvalidated band 0

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 12.0.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow's Image.merge() can dereference a null image8 plane. Validation skips the first input band, allowing a 32-bit integer or floating-point image backed by image32 storage to be merged as a narrower multiband image. A crafted IPTC file can reach this path when an application opens and loads it, or a caller can invoke Image.merge() directly with such a first band. This causes a native process crash. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Pillow: EPS load(scale) lets Ghostscript render past the decompression bomb limit

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. In versions 2.3.0 through 12.3.0, EPS rendering does not validate the scaled image dimensions before invoking Ghostscript. Applications that process untrusted EPS or PostScript files using an application-selected scale greater than one can incur excessive Ghostscript CPU and temporary disk consumption. In versions with decompression-bomb protection, the scaled output is checked only after Ghostscript has completed rendering, allowing resource consumption beyond the configured pixel limit. The amplification depends on the scale selected by the application, not an attacker-controlled scale value. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Pillow: Unbounded recursion parsing a PDF page tree or trailer chain (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-42310)

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.1.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow can exhaust resources while parsing an existing PDF during an append operation. PdfParser follows page-tree child references without cycle or duplication tracking and follows previous-trailer chains with only an exact repeated-offset guard, so deep or cyclic page trees and long chains of unique trailer offsets can exhaust the Python stack. Repeated non-cyclic /Kids references can also cause super-linear CPU and memory use. An attacker can supply such a PDF to an application that calls Image.save with PDF append enabled. This can raise an uncaught RecursionError or consume excessive CPU and memory before output is written, causing denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: filelock: WindowsFileLock ignores mode: a 0o600 lock file and the ReadWriteLock database inherit the directory ACL

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.10.0 until 4.2.1, filelock on Windows ignores the mode argument for WindowsFileLock files and the ReadWriteLock SQLite database. A lock created with mode=0o600 receives the parent directory's inheritable ACL because _open_non_reparse_fd and _nt_open do not create an owner-only security descriptor. Another local account with inherited access can read holder metadata or the lock database, modify those files where the ACL permits writes, or take the byte-range lock after release and delay later acquisitions. UnixFileLock is not affected, and mutual exclusion between cooperating processes continues to hold. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

descriptions.value: @fastify/middie is the Express-style middleware engine for Fastify. In versions from 9.0.0 through 9.3.5, the use() function joined a path-scoped middleware's mount path to the plugin scope prefix in a way that could diverge from the path Fastify's router serves, most often when the scope prefix ended in a slash, and also for array mount paths and for mount paths written without a leading slash. When the two paths disagreed, the middleware was silently skipped while the route handler still ran, so path-scoped middleware such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting could be bypassed by a single unauthenticated request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.6, and users should upgrade to 9.3.6 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router has resolved the request.

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [workflows] Escape misp-module parameter names used as
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix applies HTML output encoding (the h() helper) to the parameter name before it is used as a form label, ensuring that any HTML metacharacters in the value are neutralized and rendered as inert text rather than executable markup.
assumptions: The misp-modules service is assumed to be a component whose output can be influenced by a module developer or a compromised service endpoint; the exact attack vector for injecting a malicious parameter name is not detailed in the patch.
MISP requires authentication to access the workflow module page; PR:L is assumed based on MISP's standard access model.
The affected version boundary (< 2.5.48) is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48, 25 commits after fix); the exact first affected version is not specified.
CAPEC-1 (Reflected XSS) is the closest match; the data source is a backend service rather than a direct request parameter, but the unencoded reflection into HTML is the defining characteristic.
The h() function is assumed to be CakePHP's HTML-encoding helper (equivalent to htmlspecialchars), based on the framework context of the MISP codebase.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/WorkflowModules/Module_misp_module.php, the translateParams method was modified: the 'label' array element changed from Inflector::humanize($paramName) to h(Inflector::humanize($paramName)), wrapping the humanized parameter name in CakePHP's HTML-encoding function before it is assigned as a form label.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N – web-based, reachable over the network. AC:L – no race or special timing; the misp-modules service simply needs to return a crafted parameter name. AT:N – no manipulation of the target system required. PR:L – the victim must be an authenticated MISP user to view the workflow module page. UI:A – the victim must actively load the workflow module page for the script to execute. VC/VI/VA:N – the MISP server itself is not compromised. SC:L – the attacker can read cookies or session data in the victim's browser. SI:L – the attacker can modify the page or perform actions in the victim's session. SA:N – no elevation of security authority on the server.

capecRationale.rationale: The misp-modules service supplies parameter names that are reflected into the HTML of the workflow module page without encoding. The attacker-controlled data flows from an external source into the rendered output, matching the reflected XSS pattern. Uncertainty: the data originates from a backend service rather than a direct HTTP parameter, but the effect (untrusted data reflected into HTML without encoding) is functionally identical to reflected XSS.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The parameter name from an external service is inserted into HTML output (a form label) without HTML encoding, allowing injected markup or script to execute in the victim's browser. This is a textbook reflected XSS.

MISP contains a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the workflow module interface. Parameter names returned by the misp-modules service are rendered as raw HTML form labels on the workflow module page without output encoding. An attacker who can influence the parameter names reported by the misp-modules service can inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in the context of an authenticated MISP user's browser.

Preconditions:

- The attacker must be able to control or influence parameter names reported by the misp-modules service.

- A victim must be authenticated and view the affected workflow module page.

Impact:

- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session.

- Potential theft of session tokens, manipulation of the MISP interface, or initiation of unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Tandoor Recipes < 2.7.0 Cross-Space Permission Cache Poisoning

descriptions.value: Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.0 contains an improper cache-key design in cookbook/helper/permission_helper.py that allows authenticated users to retain stale group-based permissions across different spaces by exploiting a cache key keyed only on user id while omitting the active space, with the cached entry's TTL refreshed on every request. Attackers can create their own space to obtain an admin group designation, then switch their active space to a victim space where they hold lesser privileges, causing the stale cached admin decision to authorize elevated access and bypass group revocations or demotions across multiple permission classes and views.

cna.title: Pillow: TiffDecode returns uninitialized memory as pixels for short JPEG strips

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.3.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow can return uninitialized memory as pixels when libtiff performs a short decode of JPEG-compressed or Group 4 fax TIFF data. The _decodeStrip and _decodeTile buffers can be larger than the bytes written by libtiff, but Pillow converts the expected rows without clearing the unwritten tail. The tile path is affected from 5.3.0 and the strip path from 6.0.0. An attacker can supply a crafted TIFF to an application that loads and returns or re-encodes its pixels. This can disclose stale heap contents without memory corruption or a process crash. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

descriptions.value: Local privilege escalation vulnerability in Iperius Backup 8.8.3, due to insufficient separation between the graphical user interface running with elevated privileges and local users with low privileges. cna.title: Edgeless Systems Contrast before 1.21.0 Credential Leak via Registry Suffix Matching

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Edgeless Systems Contrast through 1.20.0 Credential Leak via Registry Suffix Matching

descriptions.value: Contrast (Edgeless Systems) before 1.21.0 performs unanchored suffix matching when selecting per-registry configuration in the imagepuller. Config.registryFor strips a single trailing dot and then uses strings.HasSuffix(hostname, fqdn) without requiring a DNS label boundary, so a registry entry such as [registries."ghcr.io."] is also applied to any host whose name merely ends in that byte sequence, including attacker-registered domains such as evilghcr.io. When an image or layer is pulled from such a sibling domain, the imagepuller sends the configured Authorization header (basic auth, registry token, or identity token), trusts the configured custom CA bundle, follows the configured mirror, and honours insecure-skip-verify (disabling TLS verification) for that host. Image integrity is not affected, as image bytes remain pinned by digest in the policy and are validated after the pull. Configurations that use a leading dot (e.g., [registries.".example.registry"]) are unaffected.

descriptions.value: MONAI through 1.6.0 contains an eval injection vulnerability in _get_fake_spatial_shape() in monai/bundle/scripts.py. The function validates shape expressions with a helper that walks the AST and only collects ast.Name nodes, rejecting any name other than 'p' or 'n', before passing the string to eval(). Expressions built solely from constants and attribute, subscript, or call nodes (for example "(1).__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()" or "int.__class__.__init__.__globals__") contain no ast.Name nodes and therefore bypass the allowlist. cna.title: Adminer before 6.0.2 Privileged-Port SSRF via host_port Regex

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Adminer before 6.0.2 Privileged-Port SSRF via host_port Regex

descriptions.value: Adminer 5.5.1 through 6.0.1 improperly parses the login 'server' string in the host_port() function in adminer/include/functions.inc.php. The port capture group requires pure digits anchored to the end of the string, so any server value with a non-digit tail fails the regex and falls back to returning the whole string as the host with an empty port. Because the privileged-port restriction in adminer/include/auth.inc.php inspects only the parsed port, the check is skipped, and the mysqli/mysqlnd client subsequently re-parses host:port from the host string and opens a TCP connection. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can reach the Adminer login page can submit a crafted value such as 127.0.0.1:80/x to make the server initiate TCP connections to arbitrary internal hosts and privileged ports before credentials are validated, enabling server-side request forgery and blind internal port scanning (connection refused vs. handshake vs. timeout acts as a liveness oracle). This is a regression that re-opens the bypass fixed in 5.5.0 (GHSA-58cq-mgw2-38m5). Fixed in 6.0.2.

descriptions.value: Froxlor 2.0.0 through 2.3.10 is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting. When a customer (the lowest-privileged authenticated role) uploads an SSL certificate for one of their own domains, the Certificates API add()/update() methods parse it with openssl_x509_parse() and store the issuer organization (issuer['O']) value verbatim without sanitization. Froxlor's table-listing renderer then emits scalar cells through Twig's `raw` filter, disabling HTML auto-escaping, so when an administrator or reseller opens Domains > SSL certificates the attacker-supplied issuer value executes as script in the privileged user's session. This crosses a privilege boundary from customer to admin and can result in full administrator account takeover; because a Froxlor admin controls webserver, DNS, and PHP configuration applied by a cron job running as root, the issue can be further escalated to command execution as root on the managed server. The issue is fixed in Froxlor 2.3.12.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: capgo.app Authentication Bypass via PostgREST customer_id Mutation

descriptions.value: capgo.app is an over-the-air update platform for Capacitor apps. In all versions prior to a fix, the row-level security UPDATE policy on the public.orgs table permits an organization admin (a user holding org.update_settings) to update the entire row, including the internal billing pointer column customer_id. The official organization update endpoint (supabase/functions/_backend/public/organization/put.ts) allowlists only a small set of editable settings fields and excludes customer_id, and the private Stripe billing route separately requires the org.update_billing permission. By sending an update directly to Supabase PostgREST, an authenticated org admin without org.update_billing can null or corrupt the organization's Stripe customer pointer, causing plan and billing checks that trust orgs.customer_id to fail and moving the organization from a valid paid plan state to unpaid/no-plan behavior. At the time of the advisory no patched version was available.

cna.title: Ghidra 9.2 through 12.1.4 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via StringManager

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Ghidra 11.2 through 12.1.4 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via StringManager

descriptions.value: Ghidra versions 9.2 through 12.1.4 contain a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in StringManager::getCodepoint when decoding multi-byte UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32 characters without validating remaining buffer length. Attackers can craft malicious binaries containing strings or constant byte stores that end in multi-byte lead units to trigger out-of-bounds reads that crash the decompiler or leak adjacent heap memory into decompiled output.

cna.title: Heym before 0.0.91 SSRF via image fetching and IPv6 validation

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Heym before 0.0.91 SSRF via image fetching and IPv6 validation

descriptions.value: Heym versions 0.0.90 and earlier contain two server-side request forgery (SSRF) egress gaps, both remediated in app/services/ssrf_guard.py in 0.0.91. First, the LLM image-edit input loader (_load_image_bytes) fetched caller-controlled HTTP/HTTPS URLs with a bare httpx.get, applying only a scheme check and bypassing the egress-pinning HTTP client; because the workflow DSL supports "imageInput": "$userInput.body.imageUrl", a webhook or API caller can choose the fetch target when a workflow author uses that expression, allowing requests to loopback, RFC1918, and cloud metadata endpoints. Second, _is_public_address unwrapped only IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, so IPv6 transition forms — the NAT64 well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96, deprecated IPv4-compatible ::x.x.x.x addresses, and 6to4 (2002::/16, classified as globally routable by Python 3.11.0 through 3.11.9) — could carry loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or cloud-metadata IPv4 destinations past both the initial URL validation and the dial-time IP pin. Version 0.0.91 routes the image loader through guard_http_url and the guarded client, evaluates NAT64 and IPv4-compatible addresses by their embedded IPv4 address, and refuses 64:ff9b:1::/48, 6to4, and Teredo (2001::/32) outright.

cna.title: Budibase before 3.45.0 Arbitrary Local File Read via OpenAPI Import

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Budibase before 3.45.0 Arbitrary Local File Read via OpenAPI Import

descriptions.value: Budibase versions before 3.45.0 fail to disable external JSON reference resolution in the OpenAPI/Swagger import validator, allowing authenticated builders to read arbitrary local files. Attackers with builder access can embed file:// references in OpenAPI specifications submitted to the import endpoint to exfiltrate sensitive files including environment variables containing JWT secrets, API keys, and database credentials.

cna.title: OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 Authentication Bypass via activation

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 Authentication Bypass via activation

descriptions.value: OpenClaw (npm package `openclaw`) before 2026.7.1 does not enforce the documented owner-only requirement for persistent `/activation` policy changes in group channels. An authorized non-owner channel sender can change whether the agent requires mention-based activation, causing the agent to respond more broadly in the group (exposing its responses to additional group traffic) or suppressing expected activation behavior until an owner restores the intended setting. The issue is fixed in version 2026.7.1.

cna.title: AIL Framework Onion Module: Non-Onion URL Accepted as Crawler Task Due to Bypassed Domain Validation

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: chg: [security] Onion module, prevent non-onion crawler task

x_patch2vuln.subject: chg: [security] Onion module, prevent non-onion crawler task
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The length-based shortcut that bypassed onion-domain validation is removed. Every extracted URL is now parsed using the standard URL domain extraction function, and the resulting hostname is validated against the existing onion-domain validation routine before the URL is added to the crawler task set. This ensures that only URLs whose hostname is a genuine .onion domain can be queued as crawler tasks.
assumptions: The affected version range is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata indicating the fix commit is 24 commits before the v7.1 tag; the exact version number of the vulnerable release is not specified in the patch.
The CVSS assumes the attacker can place crafted content in a location the AIL Framework crawler will process; the specific crawling scope and configuration are not detailed in the patch.

CAPEC-126 (Parameter Tampering) is the closest available attack pattern; the actual attack is content-based URL injection rather than classic request parameter tampering, so the mapping is approximate.

The impact is assessed as Low Integrity based on the evidence that non-onion URLs are queued as crawler tasks; broader downstream consequences (e.g., SSRF-like effects) are not evidenced in the patch and are not assumed.
The commit date (24 Sep 2026) is taken as-is from the patch metadata; no independent verification of the timeline is performed.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In bin/modules/Onion.py, the conditional block that checked len(url) == 69 and url.endswith('.onion') to shortcut domain extraction (url[7:]) without calling crawlers.is_valid_onion_domain() is removed. The code is replaced with an unconditional call to crawlers.get_url_domain(url) followed by a check that the returned domain is truthy and passes crawlers.is_valid_onion_domain(domain) before adding the domain and URL to the respective sets. Net change: 2 insertions, 9 deletions in a single file.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: Attack Vector is Network because the attacker publishes crafted content on the web that the framework crawls. Attack Complexity is Low because the attacker only needs to construct a URL of exactly 69 characters ending in .onion with a non-onion hostname. No special Adversary Techniques are required. Privileges Required is None because the attacker is an unauthenticated content publisher. User Interaction is None because the crawler processes the content automatically. The primary impact is Low Integrity on the vulnerable component: the crawler task queue is polluted with non-onion URLs, violating the integrity of the framework's target selection. No confidentiality or availability impact is evident from the patch. No subsequent component impact is identified in the evidence.

capecRationale.rationale: The attacker tampers with URL parameters embedded in untrusted crawled content to bypass the application's validation logic and inject non-onion targets into the crawler task queue. CAPEC-126 is the closest available pattern describing manipulation of input parameters to achieve unintended application behavior. The mapping is approximate because the attack vector is content-based injection rather than direct request parameter manipulation, but the core mechanism (crafting input to bypass validation) aligns with this pattern.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The URL input was validated using an insufficient heuristic (string length and suffix) that could be satisfied by non-onion URLs. The proper hostname parsing and onion-domain validation step was bypassed by the shortcut, allowing attacker-controlled URLs to be accepted as valid onion targets.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-126 Parameter Tampering

solutions.value: The length-based shortcut that bypassed onion-domain validation is removed. Every extracted URL is now parsed using the standard URL domain extraction function, and the resulting hostname is validated against the existing onion-domain validation routine before the URL is added to the crawler task set. This ensures that only URLs whose hostname is a genuine .onion domain can be queued as crawler tasks.

supportingMedia.value: The length-based shortcut that bypassed onion-domain validation is removed. Every extracted URL is now parsed using the standard URL domain extraction function, and the resulting hostname is validated against the existing onion-domain validation routine before the URL is added to the crawler task set. This ensures that only URLs whose hostname is a genuine .onion domain can be queued as crawler tasks.

descriptions.value: The Onion module in AIL Framework contained a performance shortcut in its URL extraction logic that accepted URLs as valid .onion targets based solely on a length check (exactly 69 characters) and a suffix check (ending in ".onion"), without performing proper hostname parsing or onion-domain validation. An unauthenticated attacker who could publish or control web content crawled by the framework could embed a crafted URL containing an IP address or non-onion hostname with a path ending in ".onion" that satisfied the length and suffix conditions. Such a URL would be extracted, its domain naively sliced from the string, and queued as a legitimate onion crawler task. This allowed unauthenticated content publishers to inject arbitrary non-onion targets into the crawler's task queue, influencing crawler behavior and potentially directing it toward unintended network resources. The vulnerability required no authentication, no user interaction, and only the ability to place crafted content in a location the framework would crawl. The security impact is a loss of integrity in the crawler's target selection: the framework processes and acts upon URLs that do not correspond to legitimate .onion services.

cna.title: OpenNext Cloudflare: Cache interception can bypass middleware protection for encoded paths

descriptions.value: OpenNext Cloudflare is an open Next.js adapter for Cloudflare. From 0.3.0 until 1.20.2, applications that enable enableCacheInterception, rely on middleware for access control, and have a matching cached protected route process encoded pathnames inconsistently between middleware matching and cache lookup. An unauthenticated attacker can use a percent-encoded pathname that does not match authorization middleware but decodes to the cache key of a protected route, causing cached content to be returned without authorization. Malformed encodings can also be partially decoded, allowing cache lookup to continue with a pathname that middleware did not evaluate consistently. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.2.

cna.title: Zulip: Guests can read new messages in non-subscribed public channels

descriptions.value: Zulip is an open-source team collaboration tool. In Zulip Server versions through 12.1, guest users can receive new message events for public channels outside their subscriptions. A guest can trigger the issue by registering an event queue with parameters that request messages from an unsubscribed public channel, or an existing event queue can remain affected after the guest's access to the channel is removed. The flaw discloses new public-channel messages to the guest. This issue is fixed in version 12.2.

cna.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in AIL Framework Username Timeline Tooltip

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: chg: [security] fix XSS in username timeline tooltip.

x_patch2vuln.subject: chg: [security] fix XSS in username timeline tooltip.
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix applies the existing sanitize_text() helper to the user-controlled username value (d.obj) immediately before it is interpolated into the D3 tooltip HTML string. This ensures that any HTML or script content embedded in the stored username is neutralized before DOM insertion, preventing script execution while preserving the tooltip's intended formatting (line breaks and date/time display).
assumptions: The UI:A (Active) user interaction metric assumes the analyst must deliberately hover over the specific timeline entry to trigger the XSS; passive rendering without hover is not evidenced in the patch.

The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v7.1, 29 commits after fix); the exact last affected and first fixed version numbers are not explicitly stated in the patch.

PR:N assumes the attacker does not need an account on the AIL Framework itself, only a presence in a crawled chat or forum source; if the platform requires the attacker to be a registered user to have their username crawled, PR:L might be more appropriate.
The CAPEC-1 mapping is the closest available pattern for stored XSS; no more specific CAPEC ID for 'stored XSS via imported data rendered in a tooltip' exists in the CAPEC catalog.
The sanitize_text() helper is assumed to perform adequate HTML entity encoding or equivalent neutralization; its implementation is not shown in the patch.

VC:H and VI:H reflect the sensitivity of an intelligence-analysis platform where an authenticated analyst session may contain classified or highly sensitive data; if the deployment context is less sensitive, lower impact ratings could apply.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary:
In var/www/static/js/d3/timeline_basic.js, the single line constructing the tooltip HTML was changed from tooltip.html(`${d.obj}
...`) to tooltip.html(`${sanitize_text(d.obj)}
...`). The only modification is wrapping the untrusted d.obj variable with the sanitize_text() function call at the HTML sink, leaving the rest of the tooltip template (br tags, date formatting) unchanged.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The vulnerability is in a web application accessible over the network. AC:L: The attacker only needs to craft a username with HTML/JS in a chat or forum that gets crawled; no race conditions or complex conditions are needed. AT:N: No attack on the target system is required; the malicious username is stored as part of normal data import. PR:N: The attacker does not need any account or privilege on the AIL Framework; they only need to be a user in a source chat/forum. UI:A: The victim (analyst) must actively hover over the specific timeline entry to trigger script execution. VC:H: XSS in an authenticated analyst session can expose sensitive intelligence data, session tokens, and credentials. VI:H: The attacker can perform actions as the analyst, modify data, or exfiltrate information. VA:N: No impact on availability. SC/SI/SA:N: No subsequent system impact is evidenced.

capecRationale.rationale: CAPEC-1 describes the general pattern of injecting client-side scripts into web pages via untrusted input. The patch evidence shows a stored username (untrusted input from chats/forums) being rendered into an HTML tooltip without sanitization, matching the stored-XSS sub-pattern of CAPEC-1. This is the closest and most direct CAPEC mapping for an XSS vulnerability where attacker-controlled data is persisted and later rendered in a victim's browser.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The patch inserts a user-controlled value (username from imported chats/forums) into an HTML context via D3's html() method without sanitization. The fix adds sanitize_text() at the sink, confirming the root cause is missing output encoding/neutralization of untrusted data in an HTML context, which is the definition of CWE-79 (stored XSS variant).

descriptions.value: CAPEC-1 Cross Site Scripting

solutions.value: The fix applies the existing sanitize_text() helper to the user-controlled username value (d.obj) immediately before it is interpolated into the D3 tooltip HTML string. This ensures that any HTML or script content embedded in the stored username is neutralized before DOM insertion, preventing script execution while preserving the tooltip's intended formatting (line breaks and date/time display).

descriptions.value: The AIL Framework's username timeline feature is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS). Usernames imported from chats and crawled forums are stored without character restrictions. When an authenticated analyst views the username timeline, the application renders these stored usernames into the DOM using D3's html() method in the tooltip. Because the username value (d.obj) is interpolated directly into an HTML string without sanitization, a crafted username containing HTML event handlers (e.g., ) will execute arbitrary JavaScript in the analyst's browser when the analyst hovers over the corresponding timeline entry. The attack requires the victim to be an authenticated analyst with access to the timeline view and to interact with the malicious timeline entry (hover). Successful exploitation can lead to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed within the analyst's authenticated session. The vulnerability resides in the client-side JavaScript file var/www/static/js/d3/timeline_basic.js.

supportingMedia.value: The AIL Framework's username timeline feature is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS). Usernames imported from chats and crawled forums are stored without character restrictions. When an authenticated analyst views the username timeline, the application renders these stored usernames into the DOM using D3's html() method in the tooltip. Because the username value (d.obj) is interpolated directly into an HTML string without sanitization, a crafted username containing HTML event handlers (e.g., <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>) will execute arbitrary JavaScript in the analyst's browser when the analyst hovers over the corresponding timeline entry. The attack requires the victim to be an authenticated analyst with access to the timeline view and to interact with the malicious timeline entry (hover). Successful exploitation can lead to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed within the analyst's authenticated session. The vulnerability resides in the client-side JavaScript file var/www/static/js/d3/timeline_basic.js.

cna.title: OpenClaw before 2026.8.1 Authentication Bypass via Exec Wrapper

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenClaw before 2026.8.1 Authentication Bypass via Exec Wrapper

descriptions.value: OpenClaw (npm package 'openclaw') versions >= 2026.3.22 and < 2026.8.1 contain an approval-bypass flaw in the exec approval policy: the policy could trust a command-running wrapper without inspecting the command carried in its arguments. After an operator allowlisted or permanently approved a benign wrapper invocation, a later agent turn could substitute an arbitrary inner command and execute it with the OpenClaw process's host privileges without a further approval prompt. Exploitation requires the relevant wrapper to resolve on the host and a prior operator decision allowing that wrapper. Transparent shell carriers and opaque utilities such as process monitors, tracers, namespace tools, and proxy wrappers were affected through related trust-resolution gaps. Fixed in 2026.8.1.

cna.title: Rucio: Improper Authentication via SSH Challenge Tokens

descriptions.value: Rucio is a scientific data management framework. From 1.14.0 until 35.9.1, 38.6.1, 40.4.2, and 41.1.1, validate_auth_token in lib/rucio/core/authentication.py does not distinguish short-lived SSH challenge nonces from authentication tokens stored in the same token table. cna.title: vm2 before 3.12.2 Authorization Bypass via Custom Resolver

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: vm2 before 3.12.2 Authorization Bypass via Custom Resolver

descriptions.value: vm2 before 3.12.2 contains an authorization bypass in the NodeVM external-module resolver. When an embedder configures `require.external` with a custom resolver (and `context: 'host'`), `LegacyResolver.customResolve` in lib/resolver-compat.js records the resolved module directory in `this.externals` as `new RegExp('^' + escapeRegExp(resolvedPath))`, without requiring a path separator or end-of-string boundary. Untrusted guest code can therefore require the allowlisted module (e.g. `foo`) and then require the absolute path of a non-allowlisted sibling whose path merely shares the resolved prefix (e.g. `.../node_modules/foo2/index.js`); the sibling passes `isPathAllowedForModule` and is loaded through `hostRequire`, so its top-level code runs in the host process before the exports are wrapped with `vm.readonly`, resulting in a sandbox escape and arbitrary code execution in the host context.

cna.title: capgo.app Content-Lock Bypass via r2-direct Bundle Mutation

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: capgo.app Content-Lock Bypass via r2-direct Bundle Mutation

descriptions.value: Capgo (capgo.app) contains an incomplete access-control/content-lock enforcement issue affecting all versions; no patch is available at the time of publication. The `enforce_encrypted_bundle_trigger` / `check_encrypted_bundle_on_insert` content lock in supabase/schemas/prod.sql exempts `app_versions` rows whose previous `storage_provider` is `r2-direct`, so delivery-critical columns (name, app_id, session_key, key_id, storage_provider, r2_path, external_url, checksum, manifest, native_packages) remain mutable while a row is in that state. Separately, the channel/version join used by the `/updates` endpoint (supabase/functions/_backend/utils/pg.ts) filters only deleted versions and does not exclude `r2-direct` versions, so such rows remain OTA-selectable. An attacker holding a Capgo API key with bundle write/upload permission can create or keep a bundle version in the `r2-direct` state, assign it to a channel, and then modify these fields via direct PostgREST requests, causing altered bundle metadata (for example checksum and session_key) to be served to devices through `/updates`. This bypasses the post-upload content immutability hardening added for a previous app_versions metadata-tampering issue.

cna.title: OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 Authentication Bypass via Active Memory

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 Authentication Bypass via Active Memory

descriptions.value: OpenClaw is an npm-distributed agent gateway. In versions before 2026.7.1, the global Active Memory toggle mutations could omit owner checks. An authorized non-owner external-channel sender could therefore persistently enable or disable Active Memory for the Gateway, disabling memory recall for future sessions or re-enabling global recall where the owner expected it to remain disabled. The issue is limited to persistent global on/off mutations; session-level controls and read-only status remain governed by existing command policy. The issue is fixed in version 2026.7.1. (Suggested title: "OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 missing owner authorization check on Active Memory global toggles".)

cna.title: OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 Allowlist Bypass via Workspace Shadows

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenClaw before 2026.7.1 Allowlist Bypass via Workspace Shadows

descriptions.value: OpenClaw is an npm-distributed agent runtime. In versions >= 2026.2.26 and < 2026.7.1, PowerShell command analysis on Windows hosts running in exec allowlist mode could approve an exact executable resolved from PATH but subsequently execute a same-named executable located in the workspace directory. If lower-trust content can place an executable with an approved basename into an agent-writable workspace and steer an approved PowerShell command that uses a bare executable name, OpenClaw may run the workspace file instead of the allowlisted path, executing arbitrary code with the privileges of the Gateway or node-host user. The issue does not require replacement of the approved executable itself. Version 2026.7.1 contains a fix; as a workaround, avoid bare executable names in approved PowerShell commands and keep executable files out of agent-writable workspaces.

cna.title: OpenClaw before 2026.8.1 Canvas Capability Revocation Bypass

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenClaw before 2026.8.1 Canvas Capability Revocation Bypass

descriptions.value: OpenClaw (npm package 'openclaw') versions >= 2026.5.12 and < 2026.8.1 do not immediately invalidate Canvas HTTP authorization when a paired node is revoked. Node revocation invalidates the WebSocket client, but Canvas HTTP authorization continues to accept and renew the previously granted capability until WebSocket close cleanup completes. As a result, a revoked paired node can continue exercising its Canvas capability against the capability's configured routes during the close grace period. The issue is fixed in 2026.8.1; as a workaround, restart the Gateway after revoking a node that has Canvas access.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Flowise through 3.1.4 Authorization Bypass via BullMQ Dashboard

descriptions.value: Flowise through 3.1.4 does not enforce authorization on the BullMQ admin dashboard. When the server runs in queue mode with the dashboard enabled and not in cloud mode (MODE=queue, ENABLE_BULLMQ_DASHBOARD=true, and !isCloud()), the /admin/queues mount is protected only by the verifyTokenForBullMQDashboard middleware, which validates the JWT but performs no role, permission, or workspace/organization scoping check; the mount also lies outside /api/v1/* so the global API gate does not apply. cna.title: LXC: lxc-copy host-context hostname update follows symlink

descriptions.value: LXC is a userspace interface for the Linux kernel containment features used to create and manage system containers. In LXC 7.0.0 and earlier, lxc-copy and the public liblxc clone() API can follow attacker-controlled symbolic links while updating /etc/hostname in a copied container root filesystem. The affected surfaces are lxc-copy and liblxc's public lxc_container::clone() API. The privileged cloning process must run as root. The source rootfs must be attacker-controlled or less trusted. A symlink can be placed at etc/hostname or in an intermediate component. The clone operation preserves the symlink before updating the hostname. The vulnerable write truncates and overwrites an existing file outside the destination rootfs. When root clones an untrusted container without LXC_CLONE_KEEPNAME, the copied symlink can resolve outside the destination rootfs and cause the privileged process to overwrite an existing host file with the destination container name. Unprivileged use and managers with independent cloning implementations are not affected. LXC_CLONE_KEEPNAME avoids the hostname update and therefore the affected write.
